      "query_id": "tc_0655",
      "query": "How do I make the sensor bypass system proxy and go direct to reg/detection servers?",
      "ground_truth": "Set the sensor proxy to a nonexistent localhost proxy (127.0.0.1:12345) with proxy_type set to direct in ap_configuration.json and run the personalization script. Also configure the same proxy host/port for the detection server in the UI so it falls back to direct connection.",
      "actual_answer": "To make the Cybereason sensor bypass any system proxy (including proxy lists or PAC) and connect **directly** to the **Registration** and **Detection** servers, configure the sensor to “use” a **nonexistent localhost proxy** so it fails over to direct connection.\n\n### Registration Server (package-side configuration)\n1. On the sensor package host, edit:\n   - `/opt/puppet-cybereason/manage/management/ap_configuration.json`\n2. Set the proxy values like this:\n   - `\"proxy_list\": \"127.0.0.1:12345\"`\n   - `\"proxy_type\": \"direct\"`\n3. Apply the change:\n   - `/opt/puppet-cybereason/run_personalization.sh -p`\n4. Ensure **no service is listening** on `127.0.0.1:12345` on endpoints (it must be nonexistent).\n\nResult: the sensor tries the nonexistent proxy, fails, and then connects **directly**, ignoring the machine’s configured proxies for Registration server connectivity.\n\n### Detection Server (UI-side configuration)\n1. In the Cybereason UI, go to:\n   - **System > Detection servers**\n2. Select your Detection server and enable proxy usage, then choose **Proxy list**.\n3. Set the proxy to:\n   - `127.0.0.1` port `12345`\n4. Save the changes.\n\nResult: the sensor similarly fails proxy connection and then connects **directly** to the Detection server, bypassing system proxy settings.\n\n**Note:** The Knowledge Base also states it’s not possible to override Detection server proxy settings via the command line when a Registration server is deployed—you must set Detection server proxy behavior in the UI.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000020906: \"Force Direct Connection for Sensor (Ignore Proxies)\" (v4, updated 2025-12-08T18:43:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021346: \"Best Practices for Using Proxies with the Sensor\" (v2, updated 2025-07-10T19:10:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000016912: \"Configure Proxy Connection Details\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:36:14.000+0000)\n- Article #000016902: \"Manage Server Settings\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:33:03.000+0000)",

      "query": "What log entry shows Fileless Script Analysis is blocking an app, and how do I fix it?",
      "ground_truth": "Check CybereasonActiveProbe.log for an entry showing the executable being tracked by SI protection (e.g., “si protection will track” with SE_VBSCRIPT). Fix by adding the executable from the log to Process Exclusions in Fileless Protection exclusions.",
      "actual_answer": "A Fileless **Script Analysis** block shows up in the **CybereasonActiveProbe.log** with an entry like the following, indicating the executable is being tracked by Script Analysis:\n\n- `296 INFO 2022-07-12_10:51:47 filelesscollector.cpp:457 'nwsapsetup.exe' (pid: 20540) si protection will track (sub engine - SE_VBSCRIPT)`\n\nTo fix it, add the affected executable to **Process Exclusions** for **Fileless Protection**:\n\n- Identify the blocked app’s `.exe` name from the log line above (e.g., `nwsapsetup.exe`).\n- In the **Fileless Protection exclusions**, add that `.exe` to **Process Exclusions** (allowlist it) so Fileless Protection/Script Analysis does not monitor (and block) it.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021418: \"Log Example - Script Analysis Blocks Application\" (v5, updated 2025-12-08T17:45:39.000+0000)\n- Article #000021420: \"Log Example for Fileless Protection Exclusions Blocking Applications\" (v5, updated 2025-12-08T17:46:22.000+0000)\n- Article #000021438: \"Non-Malicious Process Blocked by Fileless (PowerShell and .NET) Protection\" (v5, updated 2025-12-03T20:39:25.000+0000)\n- Article #000016859: \"Set the Fileless Protection Modes\" (v5, updated 2025-11-24T21:17:23.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0661",
      "query": "If two Linux clones share same PylumID, why does the second sensor never show online?",
      "ground_truth": "The detection server keeps the first sensor connection and refuses to establish a connection for the second machine with the same PylumID, so it never comes online.",
      "actual_answer": "If two Linux clones share the same PylumID, the second sensor may never show as online because the Detection server keeps the first connected sensor session for that PylumID and won’t establish/maintain a separate connection for another machine presenting the same PylumID.\n\nFrom the Knowledge Base examples, when a second machine with the same PylumID tries to connect, the server accepts the initial connection but effectively “wins” the PylumID for the first machine, so the second machine won’t appear as a separate online sensor in the UI.\n\nKey details from the KB:\n- In virtualized Linux environments, the sensor’s PylumID is generated from `/sys/class/dmi/id/product_uuid`.\n- If Linux VMs are mis-cloned/moved such that multiple VMs have the same `product_uuid`, they will also have duplicate PylumIDs.\n- Observed behavior includes:\n  - Only the first connected machine remains online; the second “never will be online.”\n  - In some scenarios, the UI may “flip” between two machine names with the same PylumID; in other scenarios, the second machine may not show up in the UI at all (even though the shared PylumID may be visible in exports).\n\nTo fix, Cybereason recommends addressing the duplicate `product_uuid`/duplicate PylumID issue by forcing regeneration per **“PylumId in Linux VM Machines”** (the retrieved context indicates this is the remediation path, but does not include the exact step-by-step procedure in the provided excerpts).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021425: \"Sample Behavior when Same PylumID Machines Available\" (v5, updated 2025-12-08T17:47:24.000+0000)\n- Article #000022016: \"Virtualization FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-23T19:44:15.000+0000)\n- Article #000021749: \"PylumId in Linux VM Machines\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T20:49:44.000+0000)\n- Article #000021468: \"Duplicate Sensors or Data Overrides After VM or VDI Sensor Deployment with Golden Image\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:10:50.000+0000)\n- Article #000021330: \"Considerations for Deploying a Sensor Using a Golden Image\" (v1, updated 2025-06-09T21:12:32.000+0000)\n- Article #000022428: \"Sensors on Rebuilt Machines\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:28:50.000+0000)",

      "query": "Windows sensor upgrade timing out—what policy causes it and how to fix?",
      "ground_truth": "The issue is caused by the Windows \"DisableBrowse\" policy being enabled, which blocks the installer from upgrading from its current location. Workarounds are to disable the policy (temporarily if needed) or run the installer from the original install path.",
      "actual_answer": "Windows sensor upgrades can time out due to the Microsoft Windows Installer policy **“DisableBrowse”** being enabled; it prevents the Cybereason installer from performing the upgrade from its current location, which can cause the upgrade to exceed **600 seconds** and be aborted.\n\n**How to fix (workarounds):**\n- **Disable the “DisableBrowse” policy** (recommended), or\n- **Temporarily disable it during the upgrade**, using one of these methods:\n  - **Group Policy Management** tool, or\n  - **Registry change**: toggle the key at  \n    `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Installer`\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021540: \"Windows Sensor Upgrades Are Failing\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T22:07:17.000+0000)\n- Article #000023094: \"23.2 All Versions\" (v18, updated 2026-01-27T14:08:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000023127: \"22.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-14T18:42:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000021376: \"Sensor upgrade fails with Error: Bad MSI Signature on Windows 10 - Support Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-07-10T16:58:34.000+0000)\n- Article #000022066: \"Scaled Sensor Upgrade Process - FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-18T21:08:10.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0707",
      "query": "SSO login fails w/ wrong username/password in Cybereason UI—what should I check?",
      "ground_truth": "Confirm the user has an account in the Users screen and that their Authentication method is set to SSO.",
      "actual_answer": "Check that the user account exists in Cybereason and that it’s configured to use **SSO** (not Username/Password).\n\n- **Verify the user exists**\n  - In the Cybereason UI, go to the **Users** screen and confirm the user (email) is listed.\n  - If the user does not have an account, they will get **“Wrong username or password”** when trying SSO.\n\n- **Verify the user’s Authentication method is set to SSO**\n  - In the **Users** screen, confirm **Authentication method = SSO** for that user.\n  - Cybereason enforces the configured login method:\n    - An **SSO user** cannot log in with a password, and a **Username/Password** user cannot log in via SSO.\n\n- **Check for configuration restrictions**\n  - Ensure the user does **not** have **2FA enabled** if they are set to **SSO** (2FA cannot be enabled together with SSO).\n  - Note: **admin@cybereason.com** cannot be configured to use SSO.\n\nIf these checks look correct but the issue persists, the Knowledge Base notes the specific reason can appear in the platform logs (e.g., “Perspective log”), and you may need to involve support/your Cybereason contacts to review them.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021460: \"Wrong username or password\" Error Message when Sgning in with SSO\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T22:08:13.000+0000)\n- Article #000021738: \"Cannot Access Cybereason UI - Wrong Username or Password (PIP)\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:42:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000022641: \"Single Sign-On (SSO) Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000021961: \"Single Sign-On (SSO) Troubleshooting - Important Links and Information\" (v2, updated 2025-06-20T20:15:02.000+0000)\n- Article #000021744: \"\"Oops! something went wrong\" Error Returned After Clicking 'Sign in with SSO'\" (v4, updated 2025-12-01T22:03:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000021461: \"The Cybereason UI Login Page Does Not Show 'Sign In with SSO' Option\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:42:41.000+0000)",

      "query": "How do I stop Fileless Protection flagging legit wscript.exe scripts?",
      "ground_truth": "If the script is legitimate, add the script name as a process exclusion using the \"rgx:\" prefix in the Fileless protection Process exclusions section.",
      "actual_answer": "To stop Fileless Protection from flagging legitimate **wscript.exe** script executions, add an exclusion for the specific script (or exclude the detection pattern), and ensure you’re not on a sensor version known to generate false positives.\n\n- **1) Check sensor version (possible false positive range)**\n  - If the sensor version is **21.1.282–21.1.343**, **upgrade the sensor** (this range is associated with false positives for Fileless protection).\n\n- **2) Exclude the legitimate script using a regular-expression process exclusion**\n  - Copy the **command line** shown for the detection (so you can identify the exact script name being executed).\n  - In the **Fileless protection** screen, go to **Process exclusions**.\n  - Add the script name as an exclusion using the **`rgx:`** prefix (regular expression).\n  - Reference: “Exclude processes from Fileless protection with regular expressions” (as cited in the KB article).\n\n- **3) (Optional) Exclude by detection/pattern name**\n  - You can alternatively create an exclusion using the **detection name (pattern name)**. Example given in the KB: **`amsi_as_hide_office_macro`**.\n  - Warning from the KB: excluding a pattern name **excludes that detection pattern from the Fileless Protection detection engine**.\n\nWhat’s missing from the retrieved KB excerpts: the exact UI clicks/field names for adding an `rgx:` exclusion and the command-line screenshot example (the article references them but they aren’t included in the provided context).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021517: \"wscript.exe Detected by Fileless Protection\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T22:08:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000016859: \"Set the Fileless Protection Modes\" (v5, updated 2025-11-24T21:17:23.000+0000)\n- Article #000011327: \"Configure Fileless Protection Settings\" (v5, updated 2025-12-11T16:05:32.000+0000)\n- Article #000021438: \"Non-Malicious Process Blocked by Fileless (PowerShell and .NET) Protection\" (v5, updated 2025-12-03T20:39:25.000+0000)\n- Article #000021345: \"Best Practices for Fileless Protection to MInimize Conflicts with Legitimate Processes\" (v3, updated 2025-07-16T12:20:43.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why did Infinitalk VoIP break after swapping ESET for Cybereason?",
      "ground_truth": "Removing ESET enabled the Windows Firewall service, and the firewall wasn’t configured to allow VoIP traffic, causing Infinitalk to stop working.",
      "actual_answer": "Infinitalk broke because **Windows Firewall was re-enabled during the ESET uninstall**, and the firewall **didn’t have the necessary rules/settings to allow the VoIP (Infinitalk/asterisk) traffic**.\n\nFrom the Knowledge Base:\n- Uninstalling ESET changed the **Windows Firewall service** state from **“disabled” to “enabled”**.\n- Once enabled, the firewall **blocked or didn’t accommodate VoIP traffic**, causing Infinitalk to stop working.\n- The documented fix is to **reconfigure Windows Firewall to accommodate VoIP traffic**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021763: \"VoIP Software Stops Working After ESET is Replaced with Cybereason\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T22:04:57.000+0000)\n- Article #000021895: \"May 26, 2025 Cybereason Management Console Service Interruption\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:25:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000016931: \"Enable Communication with Cybereason Servers\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:44:13.000+0000)\n- Article #000021513: \"Sensor Running on AWS or Azure Fails to Communicate with Cybereason Server\" (v1, updated 2025-06-09T21:01:30.000+0000)\n- Article #000022306: \"Cybereason Mobile Architecture\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:27:10.000+0000)\n- Article #000021556: \"Sensor Connectivity Issue with Cato Networks\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:02:48.000+0000)\n- Article #000022612: \"Cybereason On-Prem SSO Configuration - Known Issues/Limitations\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:27:10.000+0000)",

      "query": "UI says only some machines shown—how long until it clears if it's a short GC?",
      "ground_truth": "If it’s a short garbage collection cycle, the Detection Server comes back online automatically in about 5–10 minutes and the warning clears on its own.",

      "actual_answer": "The Security event log size spiked because the Cybereason sensor increases the number of Windows Security Log records when it collects Windows audit logs as part of its endpoint data collection.\n\n- **What’s happening**\n  - Cybereason sensors collect event/operation data from endpoints to help detect malicious behavior patterns.\n  - When the sensor collects **Windows audit logs** (including logs related to credential theft activity, such as **Mimikatz**), the **number of Windows Security event log records increases**, which in turn **increases disk space consumption**.\n\n- **How to reduce disk space consumption (Windows setting)**\n  1.       "actual_answer": "To stagger Cybereason sensor startup in a VDI environment (to reduce “boot storm” impact), you can enable a setting that delays the start of data collection by a randomized interval.\n\n- **Randomized startup delay option (VDI)**\n  - Sensors can be configured (across many virtual instances) to **begin data collection after a randomized amount of time—30 to 90 seconds after startup**.       "query": "How do I confirm all sensors are on the same BlocklistDB version via console/SSH?",
      "ground_truth": "SSH to the Detection server(s), open the Cyber Console, and run the ExecutionPreventionDataFromSage commands to view the output. Compare the \"Data version\" value across Detection servers; if it differs, sensors are getting different BlocklistDB versions.",
      "actual_answer": "To confirm all sensors are using the same **BlocklistDB** version, you can check the **Data version** being served by each Detection server via SSH/Cyber Console.       "ground_truth": "They were grouped by a rule that merged Suspicions sharing the same internal, company, and product names even without a shared root cause. The logic was refined so MalOps must also share the same root cause detection to be grouped.",

      "actual_answer": "The host rebooted because the sensor upgrade process uninstalled the previous sensor version **without the `/norestart` flag**, which allowed the uninstall to **schedule and initiate a reboot**.\n\n- **What the logs show (root cause evidence):**\n  - The uninstall command line ran as:  \n    `...CybereasonSensor.exe ... /uninstall /quiet` (missing `/norestart`)\n  - The uninstall then scheduled reboot-required file deletions (e.g., `Info 1903...       "query": "UI/Detection/Registration won't start, Mongo connect timeout 1000ms—what iptables rule needed?",

      "actual_answer": "Add an iptables rule to allow localhost access to MongoDB on port **27017**:\n\n- Edit iptables:\n  - `vi /etc/sysconfig/iptables`\n- Add this rule:\n  - `-A INPUT -s 127.0.0.1/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 27017 -j ACCEPT`\n- Restart and save iptables:\n  - `service iptables restart`\n  - `service iptables save`\n- Note: You may also need to restart the server to start the application correctly.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021673: \"UI/Detection/Registration Servers Not Starting with Error Message \"Timed out while waiting to connect after 1000 ms\"\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:52:42.000+0000)\n- Article #000021141: \"How to Connect a New Detection Server to the UI\" (v3, updated 2025-09-22T20:11:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000021767: \"TFA Users Unable to Connect (On-Prem)\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:42:03.000+0000)\n- Article #000021370: \"Mongo DB Useful Commands\" (v2, updated 2025-07-10T13:57:08.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "The invalid entry upload error is commonly caused by duplicate entries that differ only by case, spaces within an entry row, or an incorrect value in the 'prevent execution' column.",
      "actual_answer": "Custom reputation CSV uploads usually fail with **“invalid entry”** because the CSV contains entries the platform can’t validate.\n\nCommon causes called out in the Knowledge Base:\n- **Duplicate entries (case-insensitive)** in the CSV (e.g., `Ma1ici0us-D0Main.xyz` and `ma1ici0us-d0main.xyz` are treated as duplicates).\n- **Spaces inside a valid entry row** (extra spaces in fields can make an entry invalid).\n- **Incorrect value in the `prevent execution` column**:\n  - If the entry is based on a **SHA-1 hash**, **Domain**, **URL**, or **IP**, having `prevent execution` set incorrectly can trigger the error.\n  - The guidance is to set `prevent execution` to **false** for **SHA-1 hash**, **Domain**, **URL**, or **IP** entries (Cybereason does not prevent network-related traffic; these are informational and may trigger alerts/MalOps but not network blocking).\n\nIf the specific error is: **“Invalid entry — The file contains duplicate entries for the same key”**, it’s specifically due to **duplicated lines** in the file.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021489: \"Troubleshooting Custom Reputation List Uploads\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:46:00.000+0000)\n- Article #000021930: \"Manage Reputations FAQ\" (v4, updated 2025-08-20T17:54:50.000+0000)\n- Article #000021597: \"Errors When Trying to Upload Custom Reputation List\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:19:37.000+0000)\n- Article #000016943: \"Manage Reputations\" (v6, updated 2025-11-24T21:49:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000021736: \"Linux \"localhost\" Machine Fails to Add Custom Tag\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T19:40:42.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why does syslog show wrong hostname after reboot on AWS box?",
      "ground_truth": "One common cause is that after a reboot the server reverts to the default AWS hostname, so syslog reports that instead of the configured hostname.",
      "actual_answer": "Syslog can show the “wrong” hostname on an AWS server after a reboot because the server may revert to the default AWS hostname, and the Java process that generates/forwards syslog reads the hostname at startup and won’t update it until it restarts.\n\nFrom the Cybereason KB, the main causes are:\n- **After rebooting, the machine is set with the default AWS hostname** instead of the intended configured hostname.\n- **When Java starts, it pulls a hostname parameter from the server and does not change this value when forced to**, so syslog continues to print the hostname Java initially read.\n\nResolution options mentioned:\n- **With reboot (AWS hostname fix + reboot):**\n  - Follow the referenced AWS instructions to set the correct hostname, then **reboot** so the Java process uses the updated hostname.\n- **Without reboot:**\n  - **Verify the hostname is configured correctly** (note: the article indicates Java may still keep using the old hostname until it’s restarted/rebooted).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021571: \"Syslog Server Hostname Is Not Persistent\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:38:20.000+0000)\n- Article #000021146: \"How to Configure Syslog Forwarder on GCP\" (v3, updated 2026-01-12T17:01:45.000+0000)\n- Article #000023094: \"23.2 All Versions\" (v18, updated 2026-01-27T14:08:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000022214: \"Syslog Receiver Template - Rsyslog.conf File\" (v2, updated 2025-06-20T21:28:51.000+0000)\n- Article #000022341: \"Update the Syslog Configuration for IBM Partner Deployment\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:27:10.000+0000)\n- Article #000023132: \"24.1 All Versions\" (v14, updated 2026-03-12T16:58:35.000+0000)\n- Article #000021905: \"Syslog Forwarder Template - Rsyslog.conf File\" (v3, updated 2025-06-26T17:12:22.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "Fix empty logs by allowing UDP 514 from localhost in iptables, then save and restart iptables using the provided commands.",
      "actual_answer": "To fix blank **syslog/user audit logs** on the **Perspective (Web UI) server**, apply the firewall rule to allow local UDP syslog traffic (port 514) and restart iptables.\n\n- Run these commands on the **Perspective server** (in order):\n  1. `iptables -I INPUT 1 -p udp -s 127.0.0.1 --dport 514 -j ACCEPT`\n  2. `service iptables save`\n  3. `service iptables restart`\n\nThis addresses the known issue where logs such as `userAuditSyslog.log`, `perspective-audit.log`, and `syslog.log` are empty on the Perspective server.  \n\nWhat I found does **not** include a specific KB fix for “audit logs blank” beyond the above syslog/audit-related UI log issue; if you mean `/var/log/audit/audit.log` rotation/fill-up, that’s a different issue (auditd misconfiguration) and not specifically “blank logs.”\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021650: \"Several Logs Empty on Web UI (Perspective) Server\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:31:17.000+0000)\n- Article #000022405: \"Duplicate Syslog Messages | User Audit Logs\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:27:42.000+0000)\n- Article #000021146: \"How to Configure Syslog Forwarder on GCP\" (v3, updated 2026-01-12T17:01:45.000+0000)\n- Article #000021564: \"Server Not Rotating /var/log/audit/audit.log\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:28:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000021561: \"Syslog Files Do Not Exist in Server Logs\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:37:25.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why are signature DB versions way different across sensors when Anti-Malware signatures mode is on?",
      "ground_truth": "Signature DB versions are controlled by the sensor's operating system, so they can differ widely between sensors. On Windows, 32-bit and 64-bit editions use different version series.",
      "actual_answer": "Signature DB versions can be very different across sensors with **Anti-Malware > Signatures mode** enabled because the **Signature DB version is managed separately per operating system**, and each OS (and even Windows 32-bit vs. 64-bit) uses **different version series**.\n\n- **OS-specific versioning:** The signature database version depends on the endpoint’s operating system, so versions can vary significantly between Windows, macOS, and Linux sensors.\n- **Windows 32-bit vs 64-bit:** On Windows, **32-bit and 64-bit signature DBs are in different version series**, so endpoints on different Windows architectures may show very different DB version numbers even when fully updated.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021809: \"Sensors with Significantly Different Signature Database Versions\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T21:28:20.000+0000)\n- Article #000023127: \"22.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-14T18:42:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000016913: \"Install Sensors for Windows\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:37:08.000+0000)\n- Article #000023130: \"21.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-13T16:51:08.000+0000)\n- Article #000023124: \"23.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-18T19:49:35.000+0000)\n- Article #000021994: \"Windows Signature-Based Analysis FAQ\" (v3, updated 2025-12-02T13:56:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000016788: \"Export Sensor Metadata\" (v4, updated 2025-12-17T15:49:13.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why would a sensor show up unassigned in Cybereason UI?",
      "ground_truth": "This happens when the sensor is placed in the Default site and that site has no Detection servers. In that case, the sensor ends up without an assigned Detection server and triggers an alert.",
      "actual_answer": "A sensor shows as **Unassigned** in the Cybereason UI when it is placed in the **Default site** but that site has **no Detection servers**, so the sensor has no Detection server assignment.\n\n- Cybereason manages Detection servers **by site** (often mapped to locations or business groups).\n- During registration, sensors are assigned to the **Default site** when they **don’t match any assignment rules**.\n- If the **Default site has no Detection server**, the sensor remains **unassigned**, and the UI raises an alert (often with an **Assignment CSV** to help with assignment).\n\n**How to resolve (per KB):**\n- **Add a Detection server to the Default site**, or\n- **Assign the sensor to a different site/Detection server** (Cybereason recommends doing this quickly to maintain full coverage).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021431: \"Sensors Unassigned to a Detection Server\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:27:35.000+0000)\n- Article #000022166: \"Offline Sensors FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-17T18:55:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000021445: \"A Newly Installed Endpoint Sensor Does not Appear in the Cybereason UI\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:13:25.000+0000)\n- Article #000021927: \"Supported Capabilities for Offline Sensors\" (v2, updated 2025-06-20T21:03:26.000+0000)\n- Article #000021450: \"Sensor Cannot Verify Minion Signature\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:00:47.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why do my older sensor/probe packages keep getting replaced by newest in UI?",
      "ground_truth": "This happens when /opt/puppet-cybereason/activeprobe/packages/created.flag is missing, causing puppet to recreate packages. It can also occur if the versions directory contains non-template files, breaking customization.",
      "actual_answer": "Your older sensor/probe packages keep getting replaced because the server’s Puppet process is recreating/customizing probe packages as if they were never created, so it overwrites your older/customized packages with the latest versions.\n\nFrom the Knowledge Base, this happens when:\n\n- The file `/opt/puppet-cybereason/activeprobe/packages/created.flag` is **missing**, which causes Puppet to always recreate customized packages.\n- The directory `/opt/puppet-cybereason/activeprobe/packages/versions` contains **non-template files/folders** (for example, a backup directory), which can cause Puppet to fail the customization logic and overwrite packages.\n\nTo fix:\n- Ensure `/opt/puppet-cybereason/activeprobe/packages/created.flag` exists.\n- Ensure `/opt/puppet-cybereason/activeprobe/packages/versions` contains **only** sensor template packages (remove anything else like backup folders).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021587: \"Sensors Packages Always Overwritten with Latest Version in the UI\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:26:19.000+0000)\n- Article #000021617: \"Sensor Packages Missing after Architecture Upgrade\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:14:48.000+0000)\n- Article #000022395: \"New Sensor vs. Old Sensor for Mac Endpoints\" (v2, updated 2025-06-17T18:31:37.000+0000)\n- Article #000020929: \"How to Find and Remove Duplicate Probes from the UI\" (v2, updated 2025-10-01T21:15:06.000+0000)\n- Article #000022975: \"Upgrade Sensor\" (v4, updated 2025-11-03T12:15:26.000+0000)",

      "query": "Win Server 2019 DC sensor ignoring PAC—what install-time proxy params fix it?",
      "ground_truth": "Use the workaround to set proxy settings during installation with the provided parameters: /install /quiet /norestart AP_SIGNON_PROXY_LIST=: AP_SIGNON_PROXY_TYPE=HTTP AP_DETECTION_PROXY_AS_SIGNON=1.",
      "actual_answer": "Use install-time proxy parameters to explicitly set the proxy (workaround for the Windows `WinHttpGetProxyForUrl` behavior on Windows Server 2019 Domain Controllers):\n\n- Run the sensor installer with proxy settings during installation:\n  - **HTTP proxy example:**\n    - `/<install> /quiet /norestart AP_SIGNON_PROXY_LIST=<proxy_host>:<proxy_port> AP_SIGNON_PROXY_TYPE=HTTP AP_DETECTION_PROXY_AS_SIGNON=1`\n  - (If you need **PAC** specifically, the KB also documents this general PAC format, but the DC issue article’s workaround is to configure proxy during install:)\n    - `/<install> /quiet /norestart AP_SIGNON_PROXY_LIST=http://<pac-server>/<proxy.pac> AP_SIGNON_PROXY_TYPE=PAC AP_DETECTION_PROXY_AS_SIGNON=1`\n\nThese parameters configure the proxy at install time and (with `AP_DETECTION_PROXY_AS_SIGNON=1`) apply the same proxy configuration for both sign-on/registration and detection communications.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021411: \"Sensors Installed on Windows Server 2019 Domain Controllers Do Not Use PAC Proxy\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T21:25:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000022319: \"Sensor Platform - Overview for Support\" (v2, updated 2025-06-20T19:07:10.000+0000)\n- Article #000020906: \"Force Direct Connection for Sensor (Ignore Proxies)\" (v4, updated 2025-12-08T18:43:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021346: \"Best Practices for Using Proxies with the Sensor\" (v2, updated 2025-07-10T19:10:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000016912: \"Configure Proxy Connection Details\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:36:14.000+0000)\n- Article #000021476: \"Sensor Status Remains Offline after Sensor is Upgraded\" (v3, updated 2026-03-18T13:15:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000016904: \"Pre-installation Requirements and Instructions\" (v9, updated 2026-03-17T01:33:50.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0767",
      "query": "Sensors page says everything offline but Investigation shows online—what fixes it?",
      "ground_truth": "Put the UI server in Zabbix maintenance, restart Tomcat on the UI server, then clear maintenance. Wait about 15 minutes for Scribe to resume exporting sensor metadata.",
      "actual_answer": "This is a known UI/status mismatch: the **System > Sensors** page can show **all sensors Offline** even while the **Investigation** screen shows sensors are actually online. The Knowledge Base points to two main fixes depending on the cause.\n\n## Fix option 1 (Scribe/UI metadata export issue)\nIf the issue is caused by **Scribe (microservice)** failing to export the latest sensor metadata to the Scribe DB, do the following:\n\n- Put the **UI server** into **maintenance mode in Zabbix**\n- Restart Tomcat on the UI server:\n  1. `sudo su`\n  2. `service tomcat stop`\n  3. `service iptables stop`\n  4. `service iptables start`\n  5. `service tomcat start`\n  6. `exit`\n- Clear **maintenance mode** for the UI server in Zabbix\n- Wait **~15 minutes** for Scribe to resume exporting sensor metadata to the Scribe DB\n\n## Fix option 2 (Detection Server issue in specific versions: OutOfMemory/native thread)\nIf you see errors like **`java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: unable to create new native thread`** (and/or `ArbiterProxy... Panic! This is a bug!`) in the Detection Server `catalina.out`, Cybereason lists:\n\n- **Workaround:** Restart the **Detection Server** (per “How to Restart the Detection server (Cloud)”)\n- **Permanent fix:** apply the relevant hotfix/fixed version:\n  - Hotfix: **23.1.347**\n  - Fixed versions: **23.1.420** or **23.2.220**\n  - Affected versions include **23.2.14x+**, **23.1.34x+**, **22.1.54x**\n\n## Note (why it happens)\n- The **Investigation** screen can query multiple Detection servers (e.g., after sensor migration), which can show mixed/duplicate statuses, while **System > Sensors** reflects the current inbound heartbeat/status.\n\nIf you want, share your Cybereason version and whether you see the Scribe warning or the Detection Server OutOfMemory error—those determine which fix applies.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021770: \"Sensors Screen Showing All Sensors Offline\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:27:07.000+0000)\n- Article #000021328: \"Machine Details Display More than One Result in Investigation Screen\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:50:51.000+0000)\n- Article #000021772: \"Sensor UI Shows All Sensors as Offline\" (v2, updated 2025-09-05T20:25:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000022166: \"Offline Sensors FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-17T18:55:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000021648: \"Sensor Status is \"Online\" but Machine is Not Connected to Cybereason Console\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:20:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021447: \"Sensor is Reported as Offline Even Though the Sensor/Server Connection is Active\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:11:36.000+0000)",

      "query": "Uninstall via Add/Remove fails—what’s the likely cause and what should I do?",

      "actual_answer": "The most likely cause is that the Cybereason sensor is **password protected**, and **an uninstall password is required**—so uninstalling from **Add/Remove Programs** fails.\n\nWhat to do:\n- **Obtain the uninstall password** (if you don’t have it) by contacting **Cybereason Technical Support**.\n- **Uninstall from the command line instead of Control Panel/Add/Remove Programs** (use the uninstall password if applicable).       "query": "UI upgrade failing on Mac/Linux sensors 24.1.40-24.1.62 — what's the workaround?",
      "ground_truth": "Manually download the installer from the Sensors Overview screen to the target machine, then upgrade the sensor using the CLI (dpkg/rpm on Linux or installer on Mac).",
      "actual_answer": "For Mac and Linux sensors running versions **24.1.40 to 24.1.62**, UI-based upgrades can fail because the **sensor package file size exceeds a limit**, which prevents the new package from downloading via the UI.\n\n**Workaround**\n- **Manually download the installer** from the **Sensors Overview** screen to the target machine.\n- **Upgrade the sensor via CLI** on the target machine:\n\n  - **Ubuntu (DEB):**\n    - `sudo dpkg -i <new deb file>`\n\n  - **CentOS/RHEL/Oracle Linux/Amazon Linux (RPM):**\n    - `sudo rpm -Uvh <new RPM file>`\n\n  - **Mac (PKG):**\n    - `sudo installer -pkg /<path-to-package>/<file name>.pkg -target /`\n\nFor additional CLI upgrade details, the Knowledge Base references: **“Update Sensors with a Software Distribution Tool (via the CLI)”**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021771: \"Sensor Upgrade from the UI Fails for Sensors Installed on Mac and Linux Machines\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:23:24.000+0000)\n- Article #000021416: \"Mac Upgrade Issues Due to Certificate Changes - Support Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-08-22T21:14:39.000+0000)\n- Article #000021462: \"Last Update Status showing as Failed although Sensor Upgrade was Successful\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:38:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000022215: \"Upgrading Mac Sensors from Jan 2020\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:28:14.000+0000)\n- Article #000021540: \"Windows Sensor Upgrades Are Failing\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T22:07:17.000+0000)",

      "query": "After upgrading sensor from UI it stays offline—what setting gets lost and why?",
      "ground_truth": "The sensor’s proxy settings can be removed during a platform/UI-driven sensor upgrade. This occurs when the proxy was originally set via command-line parameters (or a proxy-embedded installer), since UI upgrades don’t preserve those parameters.",
      "actual_answer": "After a sensor upgrade initiated from the Cybereason UI, the sensor can stay **Offline** because its **proxy settings may be lost**—specifically the **Detection/Sign-on proxy configuration**—so the sensor can no longer connect to the Detection server.\n\n- **What setting gets lost?**\n  - The sensor’s **proxy settings** (e.g., the values configured via installation parameters such as:\n    - `AP_SIGNON_PROXY_LIST`\n    - `AP_SIGNON_PROXY_TYPE`\n    - `AP_DETECTION_PROXY_AS_SIGNON=1`)\n\n- **Why does it get lost?**\n  - If the proxy was originally configured **during installation via command line (or a proxy-embedded sensor installer)**, a **UI-initiated upgrade does not preserve those installation parameter settings**, causing the proxy configuration to “disappear” and leaving the sensor unable to connect.\n\n- **Version note (Windows)**\n  - This behavior is stated as **no longer relevant for Windows Sensor 23.2.500+ / 24.1.300+**, where existing proxy configuration defined in sensor configuration (registry values) is preserved during upgrade.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000022166: \"Offline Sensors FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-17T18:55:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000021927: \"Supported Capabilities for Offline Sensors\" (v2, updated 2025-06-20T21:03:26.000+0000)\n- Article #000021476: \"Sensor Status Remains Offline after Sensor is Upgraded\" (v3, updated 2026-03-18T13:15:21.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why does the Windows sensor only show online when someone logs in?",
      "ground_truth": "This happens because the proxy is set at the user-profile level on logon, and the sensor auto-detects that user-level proxy setting.",
      "actual_answer": "This happens when the sensor is picking up a **user-level proxy setting** that only exists/activates when a user logs into Windows, so the sensor can communicate (and appear “Online”) only during an active user session.\n\n- **Applies to environments where:**\n  - A **proxy is used** for Cybereason sensor ↔ server communication, and\n  - The sensor is using a **proxy configured on the OS side**, and\n  - The proxy is **enabled as part of the user profile** when logging on (local or RDP)\n\n- **Root cause:**\n  - When a user logs in, Windows applies **user-profile proxy settings**.\n  - The Cybereason sensor **automatically detects the user-level proxy**, so it connects only while that user session (and proxy setting) is active.\n\n- **KB-recommended fix (Windows, e.g., servers with infrequent logons):**\n  - **Reinstall the sensor** and provide the proxy information as a **sensor startup parameter**, e.g.:\n    - `<Sensor Installer.exe> /install /quiet /norestart AP_SIGNON_PROXY_LIST=<Proxy Server>:<Proxy Server Port> AP_SIGNON_PROXY_TYPE=HTTP AP_DETECTION_PROXY_AS_SIGNON=1`\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021477: \"Sensor Status is Online when the User is Logged On to the Machine\" (v3, updated 2026-03-19T03:00:58.000+0000)\n- Article #000021648: \"Sensor Status is \"Online\" but Machine is Not Connected to Cybereason Console\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:20:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021709: \"Sensor Not Showing as Online in Sensors Screen\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:14:00.000+0000)\n- Article #000021447: \"Sensor is Reported as Offline Even Though the Sensor/Server Connection is Active\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:11:36.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why would a WorkSpaces Windows sensor not show up in Sensors even though curl hits the server?",
      "ground_truth": "Amazon infrastructure blocks the sensor’s SSL Client Hello because it lacks the server_name (SNI) extension, preventing communication and the sensor from appearing.",
      "actual_answer": "A Windows sensor on **Amazon WorkSpaces** may not appear in **System > Sensors** even though `curl` can reach the Cybereason server because the **sensor’s SSL handshake can be blocked by AWS infrastructure when the sensor traffic is missing SNI (Server Name Indication)**.\n\n- **What happens**\n  - The Cybereason sensor initiates an SSL handshake to the Cybereason server.\n  - In Amazon WorkSpaces/AWS, a security mechanism may **block the TLS “Client Hello”** if the **SNI extension is missing** in the sensor’s handshake.\n  - `curl` succeeds because it typically **includes SNI** in its handshake, so AWS allows the connection—making it look like “connectivity is fine” even though the sensor’s TLS negotiation is being blocked.\n\n- **Recommended action (from the KB)**\n  - Use the workaround referenced in the Cybereason KB: **“Sensor Running on AWS or Azure Fails to Communicate with Cybereason Server.”**\n  - (The retrieved content doesn’t include the workaround steps themselves—only the pointer to that article.)\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021710: \"Sensor running on Amazon WorkSpaces Fails to Communicate with Cybereason\" (v2, updated 2025-12-03T21:16:34.000+0000)\n- Article #000023094: \"23.2 All Versions\" (v18, updated 2026-01-27T14:08:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000021445: \"A Newly Installed Endpoint Sensor Does not Appear in the Cybereason UI\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:13:25.000+0000)\n- Article #000023127: \"22.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-14T18:42:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000021585: \"Sensor Always in \"Not collecting\" Mode on Windows Server\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T20:59:23.000+0000)\n- Article #000023130: \"21.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-13T16:51:08.000+0000)\n- Article #000021505: \"Sensor Connectivity Issues - Troubleshooting\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:03:17.000+0000)\n- Article #000023100: \"20.2 Known Issues\" (v4, updated 2025-11-10T20:28:46.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "This behavior can happen when the Sensor was installed on the virtual machine from a golden image.",
      "actual_answer": "A common cause is deploying the Sensor from a **golden image/clone**, which can result in **multiple VMs sharing the same PylumID**—this can cause the Sensor to **connect/disconnect repeatedly** in the Cybereason UI.\n\n- **Why it happens:** Cloned VMs can inherit the same Sensor identity (PylumID), leading to data overrides and unstable connectivity behavior (including repeated connect/disconnect).\n- **What to do:** **Contact Cybereason Technical Support**—the Knowledge Base notes Support can apply a **configuration change** to address the “connects and disconnects” behavior in golden-image VM scenarios.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021499: \"Sensor on VM Connects and Disconnects\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:14:24.000+0000)\n- Article #000021468: \"Duplicate Sensors or Data Overrides After VM or VDI Sensor Deployment with Golden Image\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:10:50.000+0000)\n- Article #000023113: \"21.2 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-13T19:59:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000021680: \"Sensor Delay on System > Sensors Screen\" (v2, updated 2025-09-05T13:53:43.000+0000)\n- Article #000021772: \"Sensor UI Shows All Sensors as Offline\" (v2, updated 2025-09-05T20:25:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000022016: \"Virtualization FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-23T19:44:15.000+0000)\n- Article #000021505: \"Sensor Connectivity Issues - Troubleshooting\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:03:17.000+0000)\n- Article #000022980: \"Restart Sensor\" (v3, updated 2025-10-31T19:24:18.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "If you can see EDR data from the endpoint in the **Investigation** screen but the **System > Sensors** page shows the sensor as **Offline**, the Knowledge Base fix is to **reconfigure the site** on the Detection server.\n\n### Fix: Reconfigure the site (resolves “sensor not showing as online”)\n1. Go to **System > Detection servers**.\n2. Click **Manage sites**.\n3. **Create a new site** called **Primary**.\n4. **Assign all Detection servers** to this site.\n5. **Select all OS types**.\n6. Add regex **`.*`** (so any device name matches), then click **Test configuration**.\n7.       "query": "Why would a Cybereason sensor show Offline in UI even though netstat/logs show it's connected?",
      "ground_truth": "This can happen when the sensor-server handshake gets stuck, leaving the sensor in a limbo state. The sensor is physically connected but the connection isn’t properly applied, so the UI shows it as Offline.",
      "actual_answer": "A sensor can show **Offline in the Cybereason UI even though `netstat` and logs show a TCP/SSL connection** when the **sensor–server connection is physically up but the logical handshake/registration state is stuck**, so the platform doesn’t properly “apply” the connection and the UI doesn’t reflect it.\n\nFrom the Knowledge Base, this can happen due to:\n\n- **Handshake stuck / “limbo” state**\n  - The sensor and server are both waiting on each other (handshake not completing), so the sensor may appear **Offline** or not appear at all in **System > Sensors**, even though logs show it connected.\n- **Detection server overload / delayed responses**\n  - This behavior was observed when **overloaded Detection servers** didn’t respond to sensors in time, leaving sensors in a limbo state.\n- **Repeated hibernation attempts on the endpoint**\n  - Repeated hibernation can break the connection state and contribute to the “connected but Offline in UI” symptom.\n\nWhat Cybereason recommends (from the same KB articles):\n\n- **Upgrade to the latest Cybereason platform version** (stability/performance improvements).\n- Use the steps in **“Sensor Connectivity Issues - Troubleshooting”** to address underlying connectivity/handshake problems.  \n\nIf you want, share your Cybereason version and whether this affects many sensors at once (often consistent with server overload), and I can point you to what the KB says to collect/verify next.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021447: \"Sensor is Reported as Offline Even Though the Sensor/Server Connection is Active\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:11:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000022166: \"Offline Sensors FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-17T18:55:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000021927: \"Supported Capabilities for Offline Sensors\" (v2, updated 2025-06-20T21:03:26.000+0000)\n- Article #000021648: \"Sensor Status is \"Online\" but Machine is Not Connected to Cybereason Console\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:20:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021445: \"A Newly Installed Endpoint Sensor Does not Appear in the Cybereason UI\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:13:25.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "This error (`-2005:BD_UPD_RET_InstallFailed`) occurs when the Signature DB update **downloads successfully but can’t be installed**, and Cybereason has linked it to **disk/file-system issues that prevent deleting leftover Signature DB plugin files**.\n\n**Fix (per Cybereason KB):**\n1. **Check for leftover Signature DB plugin files** (often remains even after uninstall), e.g.:\n   - `C:\\ProgramData\\apv2\\bd_db\\2\\Plugins\\emalwareXXX`\n2.       "query": "Sensor won’t start post-install, only cellular NIC shows—what’s the fix?",
      "ground_truth": "Add or enable a non-cellular network adapter that has a physical address, then restart the sensor (taskkill /im PylumLoader.exe /F). The sensor can’t initialize using only a cellular adapter MAC.",
      "actual_answer": "If the sensor won’t start after installation and the machine only shows a **Cellular** network adapter, the sensor can’t generate a **PylumID** because it **does not support using the physical address of the Cellular network adapter**.       "actual_answer": "After an environment upgrade, if sensors aren’t receiving the Detection server/proxy information due to a UI server ↔ Registration server sync issue, the KB fix is to restart Tomcat (and iptables on the UI server) in a specific order.\n\n**Fix steps (from “Sensor Connectivity Issue after Environment Upgrade” KB):**\n\n1) **On the UI server, restart Tomcat and iptables:**\n- `sudo su`\n- `service tomcat stop`\n- `service iptables stop`\n- `service iptables start`\n- `service tomcat start`\n- `exit`\n\n2) **On the Registration server, restart Tomcat:**\n- `sudo su`\n- `service tomcat stop`\n- `service tomcat start`\n- `exit`\n\n3) **Validate:**\n- Confirm the sensor receives the **Detection server name, port, and proxy information** from the Registration server (the KB references checking this in `CybereasonActiveConsole.log`).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021699: \"Sensor Connectivity Issue after Environment Upgrade\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:02:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000021476: \"Sensor Status Remains Offline after Sensor is Upgraded\" (v3, updated 2026-03-18T13:15:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021568: \"Sensor Not Connecting to Detection Server After Installing/Upgrading to 18.1 and above\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:13:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021481: \"Sensor Fails to Recognize Operating System Proxy Settings\" (v3, updated 2026-03-17T00:08:42.000+0000)\n- Article #000021600: \"Sensors Do Not Publish Data after Upgrade\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:24:42.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "BAL rule properties disappear during editing when the rule contains **invalid syntax in an Element filter string**, specifically **unsupported characters**.       "ground_truth": "Edit purge_old_recordings.sh and change the find command to use mtime instead of ctime so old recordings are found and removed.",
      "actual_answer": "It should use **`mtime` (modification time)**, not `ctime`.\n\n- In `/opt/puppet-cybereason/manage/tools/purge_old_recordings.sh`, replace `ctime` with `mtime` in the `find` commands, for example:\n  - `RESULT=\\`find /opt/cybereason/activeprobe/ -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -mtime +${DAYS}\\``\n  - `find /opt/cybereason/activeprobe/ -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -mtime +${DAYS} | xargs rm -rf`\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021659: \"Recording Files Purging Not Working\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T20:52:58.000+0000)\n- Article #000021118: \"How to Delete all Malware Alerts\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:23:20.000+0000)\n- Article #000021113: \"How to Export Data from Mongo DB\" (v2, updated 2025-09-26T16:29:15.000+0000)\n- Article #000023683: \"Delete Malware Alerts in Bulk\" (v1, updated 2025-11-14T16:29:20.000+0000)\n- Article #000020949: \"How to Delete Malware Alerts from the Database\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:23:57.000+0000)\n- Article #000022479: \"How to Handle False Positive Detections\" (v3, updated 2025-10-02T14:53:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000020894: \"How to Manually Extract Recordings\" (v2, updated 2025-12-31T14:36:57.000+0000)\n- Article #000022901: \"Perform a Live File Search Request\" (v3, updated 2025-10-31T19:15:26.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "To confirm **Collective UUID** is turned on after enabling the feature flag, verify the following:\n\n- **PostgreSQL checks**\n  - The **`site_info`** table (not `server_site_info`) is populated.\n  - The **`collective_uuid`** column in the **Sensors** table is populated.\n\n- **MongoDB check**\n  - In the **`properties`** collection, confirm there is a document named **`metadata.collective.uuid`**.\n\n- **Log messages (optional validation)**\n  - Look for these information logs:\n    - **T**: `\"Collective UUID persisted in DB\"` and/or `\"init flow with Collective UUID already recorded in db, skipping\"`\n    - **P**: `\"triggering on change collective UUID: FF enabled = \"` and `\"triggering on collective UUID update notification\"`\n    - **Management**: `\"Initializing siteInfoSet\"`\n    - **Scribe**: `\"triggering on change site info\"`\n\nPer the KB, **no server restart or machine reboot is required**, and changes should take **~1–2 minutes** to take effect.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000022681: \"Collective UUID - Feature Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-12-03T20:53:20.000+0000)\n- Article #000022652: \"How to Add UUID in Sensor Configurations - Policy Improvements Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-12-05T21:28:19.000+0000)\n- Article #000022960: \"Set the Fileless Protection Mode\" (v3, updated 2025-10-31T20:49:29.000+0000)\n- Article #000022821: \"gRPC Connectivity Health Reporting - Feature Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-12-05T21:19:53.000+0000)\n- Article #000021177: \"Enable Collective Throttling in On-Prem Environments\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T20:41:35.000+0000)",

      "query": "Anti-Ransomware on but ransomware still runs—what two things should I check first?",
      "ground_truth": "Verify Application Control is enabled in the policy and that at least one canary file location is selected so canary files are generated on each endpoint.",
      "actual_answer": "Check these two items first:\n\n1) **Anti-Ransomware mode in the sensor policy**\n- Verify the policy isn’t set to **Detect** or **Suspend** (both are “testing only” and don’t fully stop execution).\n- For protection, set Anti-Ransomware to **Prevent** (detect + suspend + prevent future execution on that endpoint).\n\n2) **Application Control status**\n- In **Prevent** mode, Cybereason **recommends enabling Application Control**.\n- If **Application Control is disabled**, the platform may **not prevent the process from executing again in the future on the same endpoint** (even after it was detected/suspended).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000022010: \"Threat Alert - Kaseya VSA Supply-Chain Ransomware Attack\" (v2, updated 2026-01-30T17:26:59.000+0000)\n- Article #000016285: \"Configure Anti-Ransomware Settings\" (v3, updated 2026-01-12T21:58:56.000+0000)\n- Article #000011328: \"Configure Predictive Ransomware Protection Settings\" (v3, updated 2025-11-20T18:06:24.000+0000)\n- Article #000022708: \"Predictive Ransomware Protection - Feature Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000011330: \"Configure Anti-Ransomware Settings (Canary Files)\" (v2, updated 2025-11-20T18:08:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000016283: \"Behavioral Anti-Ransomware\" (v3, updated 2026-01-12T21:58:32.000+0000)\n- Article #000016854: \"Anti-Ransomware Protection (Canary Files)\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:15:55.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "Check the sensor assignment CSV for common formatting and naming issues that cause the rebalance upload/test/apply to fail:\n\n- **Duplicate FQDNs** in the file\n- **Blank cells**\n- **Invalid site names**\n  - Confirm the site names in the CSV exactly match the names shown in **Manage sites / Sites list**.\n  - If you’re using **“Default site”**, note that the **site must actually exist** in the environment—otherwise you can see errors like *“The file you uploaded is invalid”* / *“The region Default not exist…”*.       "query": "pg_dump backup on Windows runs 3x slower w/ sensor—what config workaround fixes it?",
      "ground_truth": "Create a minionhost.conf in C:\\ProgramData\\apv2 with msrpc.kill_switch_minion_conf_only set to true and msrpc_correlation.enable set to false, then restart the sensor.",
      "actual_answer": "Create a **minionhost.conf** file to disable the MSRPC correlation/data collection behavior that can conflict with `pg_dump`, then restart the sensor.\n\n- **1) Create this file:**  \n  `C:\\ProgramData\\apv2\\minionhost.conf`\n\n- **2) Add the following content:**\n  ```json\n  {\n    \"msrpc.kill_switch_minion_conf_only\" : \"true\",\n    \"msrpc_correlation.enable\" : \"false\"\n  }\n  ```\n\n- **3) Restart the sensor** (example command):  \n  ```\n  taskkill /im minionhost.exe /F & taskkill /im PylumLoader.exe /F\n  ```\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021575: \"Postgres DB Backup ( pg_dump ) is Slow\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T20:48:48.000+0000)\n- Article #000021514: \"Sensor Clashes with 3rd-Party Backup Software, i.e. VEEAM, MoveIT\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:01:43.000+0000)\n- Article #000023124: \"23.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-18T19:49:35.000+0000)\n- Article #000020842: \"Configure a Windows Computer to Generate a Memory Dump File\" (v3, updated 2025-11-25T21:45:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000023094: \"23.2 All Versions\" (v18, updated 2026-01-27T14:08:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000023127: \"22.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-14T18:42:18.000+0000)",

      "query": "Linux VM sensors keep swapping names but same PylumID—what causes that?",
      "ground_truth": "It’s caused by duplicate /sys/class/dmi/id/product_uuid values from VM creation/migration misconfiguration, leading to duplicated PylumIDs.",
      "actual_answer": "This happens when **two (or more) Linux VMs end up with the same PylumID**, so the platform treats them as the *same* sensor and the UI appears to “swap” the machine name while keeping the same PylumID.\n\n**Cause (Linux VMs):**\n- For Linux VMs, the sensor generates the PylumID based on **`/sys/class/dmi/id/product_uuid`**.\n- If the virtualization/cloning process results in **duplicate `product_uuid` values** across multiple VMs (for example, a VM was *moved* rather than properly copied/cloned and retained the original UUID), then multiple VMs will share the same PylumID.\n- When both VMs are running, you can see behavior like:\n  - A sensor appears briefly, then is replaced by another sensor name **with the same PylumID**.\n  - In some cases, only the first VM to connect stays online; the other may fail to connect.\n\n**What’s missing from the context:**\n- The retrieved articles explain the cause and symptoms, but do not include detailed, step-by-step remediation in the excerpts (they reference following the “PylumId in Linux VM Machines” steps to fix).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021749: \"PylumId in Linux VM Machines\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T20:49:44.000+0000)\n- Article #000021425: \"Sample Behavior when Same PylumID Machines Available\" (v5, updated 2025-12-08T17:47:24.000+0000)\n- Article #000021468: \"Duplicate Sensors or Data Overrides After VM or VDI Sensor Deployment with Golden Image\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:10:50.000+0000)\n- Article #000021449: \"Duplicate Machines/Sensors Appear in the UI\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:09:58.000+0000)\n- Article #000021330: \"Considerations for Deploying a Sensor Using a Golden Image\" (v1, updated 2025-06-09T21:12:32.000+0000)\n- Article #000022016: \"Virtualization FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-23T19:44:15.000+0000)",

    {
      "query_id": "tc_0825",
      "query": "Getting 'policy sent to 0 sensors' when changing a sensor policy—why?",
      "ground_truth": "It happens because the sensor is in a group. If the group already has a policy, you can’t change that sensor’s individual policy.",
      "actual_answer": "This happens when the sensor is assigned to a **sensor group that already has a policy assigned**—in that case, Cybereason won’t let you change the policy at the individual sensor level, so the UI shows **“Policy was sent to 0 sensors.”**\n\nWhat you can do (per the KB):\n- **Option A:** Change the **group policy** to the policy you want.\n- **Option B:** Remove the machine/sensor from that group (it becomes **Unassigned**), then assign the policy to the sensor individually.\n- **Option C:** Create a **new group**, assign the desired policy to that group, and move the sensor(s) into it.\n\nNote: Cybereason documentation also states you can only assign a policy to an individual sensor if:\n- The sensor is in the **Unassigned** group, **or**\n- The sensor’s group **does not have** an assigned policy.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021708: \"Policy Sent to 0 sensors - Sensor Groups\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T20:48:23.000+0000)\n- Article #000021704: \"Policy Not Showing the Number of Sensors Assigned\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T20:47:56.000+0000)\n- Article #000021897: \"Sensor Policies FAQs\" (v4, updated 2025-08-13T11:40:38.000+0000)\n- Article #000016781: \"Sensor Policies\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T20:38:03.000+0000)\n- Article #000021928: \"Best Practices for Sensor Policy Configurations\" (v2, updated 2025-06-11T14:13:43.000+0000)\n- Article #000016791: \"Assign Sensor Policies\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T20:48:06.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "The issue is caused by a problem with installed OS packages. Fix it by running the provided bash script to uninstall google-auth-oauthlib, remove the google package directory, and unzip the protobuf egg, then verify by importing google.protobuf without errors.",

      "actual_answer": "This behavior is typically caused by one of two known issues in the Cybereason platform:\n\n- **Archived sensors are included in the policy “Assigned sensors” / “Non compliant sensors” counts**, but **archived sensors do not appear** in the Sensors screen results when you click the count.  \n  - **Cause:** The policy screen counts are incorrectly including archived sensors, creating a mismatch when drilling in.\n  - **Fix:** Cybereason Support can apply a “minimally invasive” fix—open a support case to have it reviewed/applied.\n\n- **A 500-item query limit can break the drill-down list (showing 0 or only a few sensors) when clicking the sensor count**, especially in environments with **more than 500 sensors total**.  \n  - **Cause:** Due to a **query limit of 500**, if there are more than 500 sensors, the query may return **0 sensors** when you click the policy’s sensor count.\n  - **Fix:** Upgrade Microservices (as described in the KB article “Policy Not Showing the Number of Sensors Assigned”;       "actual_answer": "For **Fileless Protection** exclusions, you can use **either** the **.exe name** or the **full path**—it depends on how specifically you want to scope the exclusion.\n\n- **Exclude by process name (common):**  \n  Enter just the executable name **including the extension**, e.g. `processname.exe`.\n\n- **Exclude by full path (more specific):**  \n  Enter the path **with the required `path:` prefix**, e.g. `path:c:\\temp\\file.exe`.  \n  - Path exclusions **can be regex-based** (e.g., `path:c:\\john\\.*\\example.exe`).\n  - Note: You **cannot** use **2-byte letters (e.g., Japanese characters)** or **underscores (_)** in **regex-based path exclusions**.\n\nIf you tell me whether you want to exclude **all instances of a process** (any location) or only a **specific installation path**, I can suggest which format to use.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000016863: \"Add Exclusions from NGAV Protection\" (v6, updated 2025-11-24T21:18:48.000+0000)\n- Article #000016858: \"Add Exclusions from NGAV Protection (Legacy)\" (v7, updated 2025-12-11T16:07:24.000+0000)\n- Article #000022785: \"Fileless Protection Enhancements - Feature Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-12-05T20:42:07.000+0000)\n- Article #000021410: \"Fileless Protection Exclusions Examples\" (v6, updated 2025-12-10T20:37:20.000+0000)\n- Article #000011327: \"Configure Fileless Protection Settings\" (v5, updated 2025-12-11T16:05:32.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0836",
      "query": "WebApp URL down w/ cert init error—what’s the fix for bad server.jks?",
      "ground_truth": "Back up the existing server.jks on the WebApp server, then copy the server.jks from the Registration/Detection server to the WebApp server. Update server.xml to match the certificate password and enable the custom certificate setting, then restart/reconfigure.",
      "actual_answer": "Fix the “Failed to Initialize connector” WebApp URL/certificate init error by replacing the bad `server.jks` on the WebApp server with a known-good `server.jks` (from a Registration/Detection server), then ensure Tomcat and the management facters config reference the correct keystore password and that the custom certificate setting is enabled.\n\n### Procedure (replace bad `server.jks`)\n1. **On the WebApp server, back up the current keystore:**\n   - `mv /opt/puppet-cybereason/ssl/server.jks /opt/puppet-cybereason/ssl/server.jks.bck`\n\n2. **On a Registration/Detection server, output the working keystore in base64:**\n   - `base64 /opt/puppet-cybereason/ssl/server.jks`\n   - Copy the full base64 output.\n\n3. **On the WebApp server, recreate the keystore from the base64 output:**\n   - `echo \"<base64 output>\" | base64 -d > /opt/puppet-cybereason/ssl/server_new.jks`\n\n4. **Update Tomcat to use the correct keystore password (must match the source server.jks password):**\n   - Edit: `vim /opt/apache-tomcat-8.5.5/conf/server.xml`\n   - Update the keystore password value to match the password used by the Registration/Detection server’s `server.jks`.\n\n5. **Make the change permanent by enabling the custom certificate configuration in the Management Facters file:**\n   - `vim $MFFILE`\n   - Change:\n     - `configured_custom_certificate => disabled`\n     - to `configured_custom_certificate => enabled`\n\n6. **Restart/reconfigure services:**\n   - `service tomcat stop; /opt/puppet-cybeerason/recinfigure.sh`\n\n7. **Verify:**\n   - Confirm the WebApp UI is accessible again and the error is gone.\n   - Re-check `server.xml` and `$MFFILE` to ensure the keystore password and custom certificate setting are correct.\n\n### What caused it (per KB)\n- The Puppet agent sometimes creates `server.jks` incorrectly (trust stores not added), which breaks certificate verification and prevents proper redirect to port **10443**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021605: \"On-Prem WebApp Certificate Error \"Failed to Initialize connector\"\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:39:55.000+0000)\n- Article #000017311: \"Configure Servers\" (v3, updated 2025-11-14T19:39:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021176: \"How To Replace Internal Certificates in Private Infrastructure Protection\" (v2, updated 2025-12-22T15:11:00.000+0000)\n- Article #000020927: \"How to Change the UI Server Certificate for On-Prem Environments\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:09:25.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0845",
      "query": "Why do NAS file servers slow down when Cybereason sensors hit them?",
      "ground_truth": "Cybereason services run as local NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM and may not have permission to access the NAS. This floods the NAS with access denied events, causing performance degradation.",
      "actual_answer": "NAS file servers can slow down because Cybereason sensor services run under the **local `NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM`** account, which often **does not have permission to access NAS shares**. When the sensor’s file-hashing/file-scanning collectors attempt to access the NAS anyway, the NAS can get **flooded with “access denied” events**, which leads to performance degradation.\n\nFrom the KB article, the collectors identified as causing the problematic NAS traffic were:\n- `FileScanCollector`\n- `NetworkFileHashingCollector`\n\nThe KB notes this is fundamentally a **permissions/networking issue** (sensor access to the NAS). Workarounds mentioned include:\n- **Grant Cybereason access** to the NAS drive/share so access attempts don’t generate errors.\n- Configure drives the sensor cannot access to be put on a **10–30 minute block list** (so the sensor won’t scan that drive for that period, then rechecks permissions).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021712: \"NAS File Server Performance Degradation\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:25:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000023124: \"23.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-18T19:49:35.000+0000)\n- Article #000023127: \"22.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-14T18:42:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000023113: \"21.2 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-13T19:59:31.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "Restart iptables on the Ansible server, then restart the sm-management service on the Micro-Services server (or restart the management containers). If it still persists, restart the WebApp (Tomcat) server.",
      "actual_answer": "This typically happens in **On-Prem** deployments when the UI can’t reach the **Management Microservice** (port **8088**)—so **no policies (including Default) appear** and creating a policy returns **“An unknown error occurred.”** A separate (and common) cause of the same error is hitting the **maximum policy limit (50 by default)**.\n\n### Fix #1 (On-Prem): Restore connectivity to Management Microservice (8088)\nSymptoms in the KB:\n- Policies page shows **no policies at all** (not even **Default**)\n- Creating a policy fails with **“An unknown error occurred”**\n- Catalina logs show **Failed to get template** / gRPC **UNAVAILABLE**\n- Telnet from UI server to MS server on **8088** is **connection refused**\n- Cause: **iptables on the Ansible server** blocking the connection\n\nDo this:\n1. **On the Ansible server**, restart iptables:\n   - `service iptables restart`\n2. **On the Micro-Services server**, restart the management service:\n   - `restart sm-management service`  \n   **OR**\n   - `docker-compose stop management`\n   - `docker-compose start management`\n3. If still not resolved, **restart the WebApp (Tomcat) server**:\n   - `service tomcat stop`\n   - `service tomcat start`\n\n### Fix #2: Check whether you hit the policy limit (50)\nIf policies *do* appear in the list (many policies exist), the “unknown error” can be due to the **max allowed policies per database** being exceeded (**50 by default**).       "ground_truth": "During environment upgrades, the Auth0 alignment Jenkins job can create a new Auth0 entry without checking existing apps, causing duplicate entries and triggering the mismatch alert.",
      "actual_answer": "You get the **“Mismatch in Auth0 and Vault values”** alert after an environment upgrade because the **Auth0 alignment Jenkins job may create a new Auth0 application entry without checking for an existing/previous one**.\n\n- During upgrades, the alignment job can **create a duplicate Auth0 application entry**\n- This **duplication** leads to **different Auth0 vs Vault values** being detected, which triggers the mismatch alert\n\n**KB-listed resolution**\n- **Delete the old Auth0 application entry** in the Auth0 management console (the outdated/previous application entry).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021674: \"Mismatch in Auth0 and Vault Values\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:14:49.000+0000)\n- Article #000021744: \"\"Oops! something went wrong\" Error Returned After Clicking 'Sign in with SSO'\" (v4, updated 2025-12-01T22:03:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000021110: \"An Error has Occurred - Cannot Get Rules\" Error Message in UI When Accessing Rules\" (v2, updated 2025-09-11T18:02:11.000+0000)\n- Article #000021307: \"Address Post Upgrade Configuration Issues\" (v2, updated 2026-01-12T19:21:45.000+0000)\n- Article #000021635: \"Sensor Upgrade Fails with Error Message \"MsiSendFail\" in Detection Server catalina.out Log\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T22:00:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021520: \"Sensor Install or Upgrade fails with the VerifyFileCertification Error on Versions Prior to 22.1.248 or 23.1.50\" (v3, updated 2026-02-06T12:24:53.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "Linux file events aren’t currently collected, so manually created files won’t appear in file investigation queries. You can only look for the creating process (e.g., touch, vi) instead.",
      "actual_answer": "A manually created file on a Linux machine may not appear in an Investigation **file query/search** because **Cybereason currently does not collect file events on Linux**.\n\n- Example: if you run `touch <filename>`, Cybereason can show:\n  - the **process** `touch` and its **command line** (`touch <filename>`)\n- But the **file query** will return **no results** for that created file because the platform lacks Linux file event telemetry.\n\n**Workaround**\n- Investigate the **process that created the file** (e.g., `touch`, `vi`, etc.) and use its process/command-line details to confirm the file creation activity.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021654: \"Manually Created File on Linux Machine Not Seen in Investigation Query\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:11:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000019354: \"File Search with YARA Rules\" (v4, updated 2026-03-06T14:17:58.000+0000)\n- Article #000022774: \"File Search for Linux - Feature Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-12-05T19:56:48.000+0000)\n- Article #000016711: \"Search for Files on Machines\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T17:43:38.000+0000)\n- Article #000016830: \"Analyze AI Hunt Malops\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:07:28.000+0000)\n- Article #000016950: \"Download a File for Analysis During Investigation\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:52:07.000+0000)\n- Article #000021910: \"File Search, File Browse and File Download FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-16T15:35:40.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why do tons of canary folders keep duplicating in one directory?",
      "ground_truth": "Cybereason creates a new canary folder whenever an existing canary folder is modified. This is typically caused by an application writing to the canary folders.",
      "actual_answer": "Tons of canary folders duplicate in one directory because a third-party application is modifying or writing to an existing canary folder, and the Cybereason platform responds by creating a new canary folder when it detects modification of an existing one.\n\nTo identify and stop the cause:\n- **Inspect the canary folders for clues**\n  - Open the folders and look for recognizable files that indicate an application is using them (example from the KB: a hidden **“.dropbox”** file suggests Dropbox activity).\n- **Use Windows Resource Monitor to find the process**\n  - Open **Microsoft Resource Monitor**\n  - Search **Associated Handles** for the canary folder name (e.g., the folder’s random-looking name) to identify which process has a handle open to it.\n- **Remediate**\n  - Reconfigure or prevent the responsible application from modifying the canary folders.\n  - After stopping the modification, **remove the duplicated canary folders** from that directory; Cybereason will recreate canary folders as needed.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021510: \"Many Canary Folders in a Single Directory\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:12:13.000+0000)\n- Article #000021432: \"Canary Files Appearing in Shared Network Folders\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:41:26.000+0000)\n- Article #000021521: \"Canary Files Being Synchronized to Cloud Storage\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:42:01.000+0000)\n- Article #000016856: \"Canary Files\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:16:19.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "It’s expected behavior: the alert is triggered by a .NET floating module detected in an EXE’s memory, not an actual PowerShell process. That’s why it’s classified as PowerShell/.NET.",
      "actual_answer": "A “PowerShell execution” MalOp can appear **even when no `powershell.exe` process exists in the Attack Tree** because the detection may be tied to **PowerShell & .NET protections identifying a floating .NET module in memory**, not an actual PowerShell process.\n\n- **By design behavior:** If the MalOp shows **“Detected by PowerShell & .NET protection (ATT&CK: Execution - PowerShell)”**, it may be triggered by a **.NET floating module** found in the memory of an EXE.\n- **What’s being detected:** The platform detects a **module floating in memory** (fileless-style behavior) that was **written in .NET**, so it classifies the MalOp as **PowerShell/.NET** even though **no PowerShell process is present**.\n- **Version note:** This behavior was introduced in **version 19.0** (it did not exist in 18.x).\n- **How to tune it (if needed):**\n  1. Go to the relevant **Sensor Policy**\n  2. Open **Fileless Protection**\n  3.       "actual_answer": "You can find the **Behavioral Document Protection rule IDs that triggered** in different logs depending on whether the feature is running under **AV** or under the **sensor**.\n\n- **If Document Protection is running under AV (Signature AV enabled):**\n  - The triggered rule IDs appear in the **AV log**.\n  - Example log field: **`DocumentRules:`** followed by IDs (e.g., `doc_obf_19;doc_aut_11;doc_mal_04`).\n\n- **If Document Protection is running under the sensor:**\n  - The triggered rule IDs appear in the **sensor log**.\n  - Cybereason notes the rule IDs “can be found today on the sensor log or the AV log (depending on where the module runs).”\n\nHow to tell which “umbrella” you’re under (AV vs sensor), per the KB:\n- The feature **prefers to work under AV** because it has broader visibility.\n- **Sensor-only operation** occurs in the specific case: **`SignatureAV=OFF` AND `BehavioralDocumentProtection=Detect`** (detect only, more limited visibility).\n\nWhat I didn’t find in the provided KB excerpts:\n- The exact **file path(s)** / exact UI steps to download the AV vs sensor logs (only that the rule IDs are visible in those logs, and an example from AV logs).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000011329: \"Rule-Based Behavioral Document Protection Settings\" (v2, updated 2025-11-20T18:07:56.000+0000)\n- Article #000022654: \"Behavioral Document Protection - Rule ID Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-12-03T19:59:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021182: \"Disable Specific Detection Rules via Advanced Sensor Options\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T20:38:03.000+0000)\n- Article #000020832: \"Retrieve Rule IDs for Behavioral Document Protection Exclusions\" (v2, updated 2026-01-08T12:46:07.000+0000)\n- Article #000022988: \"Query Sensors\" (v4, updated 2025-11-21T20:09:34.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0866",
      "query": "Why does Investigation show two sensor statuses/timestamps but System>Sensors only one?",
      "ground_truth": "This is expected behavior. Investigation queries all Detection servers with sensor data, so after a migration it can show info from both the old and current server while System > Sensors shows only the current status.",
      "actual_answer": "This is **by design**: **System > Sensors** shows the sensor’s **current heartbeat** status, while the **Investigation** screen can show **multiple records** if the sensor’s data exists on more than one Detection server (for example, after a sensor migration).\n\n- **System > Sensors**\n  - Displays the **inbound heartbeat message** from the sensor.\n  - Shows **one** (current) sensor status.\n\n- **Investigation screen (Machine details / Sensor Properties)**\n  - Displays data **published by the sensor** and the UI **queries all Detection servers** that have information about that sensor.\n  - If the sensor was **migrated to a different Detection server**, Investigation can show **two results/timestamps**:\n    - **Offline/older timestamp** for the **former** Detection server record\n    - **Online/current timestamp** for the **current** Detection server record\n  - This can also cause the **“Is connected to Cybereason”** field to show both **True** and **False** values for the same machine.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021648: \"Sensor Status is \"Online\" but Machine is Not Connected to Cybereason Console\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:20:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021328: \"Machine Details Display More than One Result in Investigation Screen\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:50:51.000+0000)\n- Article #000022501: \"Mismatch - System/Sensors vs  investigation page - Get the Sensor Population\" (v5, updated 2025-12-03T20:14:23.000+0000)\n- Article #000021447: \"Sensor is Reported as Offline Even Though the Sensor/Server Connection is Active\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:11:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000023094: \"23.2 All Versions\" (v18, updated 2026-01-27T14:08:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000021406: \"Why Does the Investigation Screen Display Different Metadata for Similar Files on Different Sensors?\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:56:01.000+0000)",
