      "query_id": "tc_0865",
      "query": "Why aren't detected malicious files moving to quarantine on Windows sensors?",
      "ground_truth": "Quarantine can fail because the SYSTEM account lacks the required NTFS permissions on the file or its folder, preventing Cybereason from moving it to the Quarantined folder.",
      "actual_answer": "Detected malicious files may not move to the **Quarantine** folder on Windows sensors mainly due to **permissions** or **known product/OS limitations/issues**, even when your policy is set to quarantine.\n\nCommon causes (and what to check)\n- **SYSTEM account lacks NTFS permissions (most common)**\n  - If the **SYSTEM** user doesn’t have **Modify** or **Full Control** on the malicious file and/or its containing folder, Cybereason cannot move the file to quarantine.\n  - Fix: Ensure **SYSTEM** has **Modify** or **Full Control** on the file/folder. (See: *Malicious Files Failed to Quarantine*)\n\n- **Windows Server Folder Redirection limitation**\n  - On **Windows Servers**, if **Folder Redirection** is enabled, files detected in redirected folders **are not quarantined**, even if Quarantine mode is selected. (See: *NGAV – Known Limitations*)\n\n- **Known issue in some versions where “prevent” worked but quarantine failed**\n  - Cybereason release notes state that **at times**, when Anti-Malware mode was set to **Quarantine**, the file was **prevented successfully but quarantine failed**; this was later **resolved** (notably referenced in **23.1** and **23.2** release notes for Windows).  \n  - If you’re on an older sensor version affected by this issue, upgrade may be required. (See: *23.1 All Versions*, *23.2 All Versions*)\n\nValidation points\n- Quarantined files (when successful) are moved to:\n  - `C:\\ProgramData\\apv2\\Quarantine` (See: *Configure Anti-Malware*)\n- Note: The UI does **not** allow retrieval of quarantined files. (See: *Configure Anti-Malware*)\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021492: \"Malicious Files Failed to Quarantine\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:51:32.000+0000)\n- Article #000011323: \"Configure Anti-Malware\" (v3, updated 2025-11-20T18:03:48.000+0000)\n- Article #000016845: \"NGAV - Known Limitations\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:12:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000023127: \"22.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-14T18:42:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000023113: \"21.2 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-13T19:59:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000023136: \"Version 19.2 Release Notes\" (v5, updated 2025-11-20T22:41:56.000+0000)\n- Article #000023124: \"23.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-18T19:49:35.000+0000)\n- Article #000023094: \"23.2 All Versions\" (v18, updated 2026-01-27T14:08:31.000+0000)",

      "query": "On macOS Mojave, why isn't Cybereason Mac AV cleaning malware in FDA-protected folders?",
      "ground_truth": "Because Full Disk Access for Mac AV isn’t enabled on Mojave, the AV can’t detect or disinfect malware in FDA-protected paths.",
      "actual_answer": "On macOS Mojave, Cybereason Mac AV won’t detect or disinfect malware in folders protected by **Full Disk Access (FDA)** if **Full Disk Access for Mac AV isn’t enabled**.\n\nFrom the Knowledge Base, the cause is that the **Mac AV component (`com.cybereason.av`) hasn’t been granted FDA permission**, so it can’t access those protected paths to scan/clean them.\n\nTo fix (enable FDA for Mac AV on Mojave):\n\n1. Open **System Preferences** > **Security & Privacy**.\n2. Click the **Lock** icon to allow changes (enter credentials if prompted).\n3. Go to **Privacy** tab > **Full Disk Access**.\n4. In Finder, browse to:  \n   `/Library/PreferencePanes/ActiveProbe.prefPane/Contents/MacOS`\n5. Locate **`com.cybereason.av`**.\n6. Drag **`com.cybereason.av`** into the **Full Disk Access** list.\n\nIf Mac AV still can’t detect/disinfect in FDA-protected paths after this, the KB advises contacting **Cybereason Technical Support**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021593: \"Mac AV Does Not Disinfect Malware in Paths Protected by Full Disk Access on Machines Running Mojave\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:48:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000022035: \"Cybereason Mac Support FAQ\" (v3, updated 2025-06-24T17:15:34.000+0000)\n- Article #000023130: \"21.1 All Versions\" (v5, updated 2025-11-13T16:51:08.000+0000)\n- Article #000021444: \"Mac AV Does Not Prevent Malware After Installation\" (v2, updated 2025-07-17T21:40:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000019413: \"Use the Anti-Malware > Signatures Mode (AV) for macOS\" (v4, updated 2026-03-06T15:54:20.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why would the Linux sensor show outbound to DNS/NTP/LDAP ports—expected or suspicious?",
      "ground_truth": "This is expected behavior. The sensor doesn’t directly open those ports; the OS may create the connections indirectly due to sensor API calls.",
      "actual_answer": "This is **expected behavior** in some environments and is **not inherently suspicious**.\n\n- **DNS (port 53):** Can occur when the sensor calls OS APIs that trigger **name resolution** (for example, resolving the Cybereason server or sign-on server).       "query": "How do I check current retention on a detection server?",
      "ground_truth": "Run `restTR | grep -i \"Oldest\"` and compare the process element timestamp to the server’s current time to determine retention.",
      "actual_answer": "To check the current retention on a Detection Server, compare the “Oldest elements” timestamps to the server’s current time.\n\n**Methods:**\n\n1) **From the Detection Server CLI**\n- Run:\n  - `restTR | grep -i \"Oldest\"`\n- Review the output line **“Oldest elements”** (and specifically the element you care about, e.g., **Process**).  \n- The time difference between the server’s current time and the element’s “oldest” timestamp indicates the current retention for that element.\n\n2) **From the UI (/rest/ping)**\n- Log in to the customer UI.\n- Change the URL suffix to: **`/rest/ping/`**\n- On the page, search for **“Oldest elements”**.\n- The date shown per element is the oldest retained entry; compare it to “now” to determine retention.\n\n**Note:** If you don’t have access to `/rest/ping`, you may need to change feature flags or contact NOC to extract this information.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021630: \"Investigate Low Retention Rates in the Detection Server\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:35:35.000+0000)\n- Article #000022456: \"Detection Cases Unified Playbook\" (v2, updated 2025-06-13T17:18:39.000+0000)\n- Article #000021006: \"How to Check Data Retention Settings\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:14:34.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "Adding a file hash to the blocklist only generates a Malop and does not stop execution. To prevent it from running, enable Application Control and mark the item for prevention.",
      "actual_answer": "A hash can still run even if it’s on the **blocklist** because **blocklisting alone does not prevent execution**. What actually stops the file is **Application Control**, and only when the hash/file is **marked for prevention** and Application Control is **enabled**.\n\n- **Why it still runs**\n  - Adding a hash to the **blocklist** will generate a Malop for detections, but **does not automatically block execution**.\n  - If the hash is blocklisted but **not marked for prevention**, Cybereason will alert (Malop) but the file may still execute.\n  - Also, prevention is **only on execution**, not on access (e.g., copying a file won’t be prevented).\n\n- **What actually stops it**\n  - **Application Control** prevents execution **only for items marked for prevention**.\n  - When Application Control is enabled and the item is marked for prevention:\n    - The file is **prevented from executing**\n    - A **Malware Alert** is generated\n    - An **Endpoint Protection Malop** is generated\n\n- **Where you can mark a file for prevention**\n  - From the **Malop details** screen\n  - From the **Investigation** screen\n  - From the **Reputation** screen\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021528: \"Application Control Repeatedly Prevents an Application from Running\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:21:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021557: \"File on the Blocklist Still Running\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T19:26:06.000+0000)\n- Article #000021126: \"Verify the Blocklist/Allowlist Hash is Updated on All CR Components\" (v2, updated 2026-01-08T19:17:39.000+0000)\n- Article #000021797: \"Which Cybereason Components Support Hash-based Allow/Blocklisting?\" (v2, updated 2025-07-08T21:49:17.000+0000)\n- Article #000022739: \"SHA-1 and SHA-256 Prevention Support - Feature Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)",
      "correctness": 5,

Adds extra details (execution vs access, malware alert/endpoint protection malop, UI locations) not present in the reference, but they don’t contradict it.",

      "actual_answer": "A **“Failed to connect”** status for a **Detection server** on the **System > Servers** screen means the **Detection server failed to connect to the WebApp server**.\n\nCommon reasons called out in the Knowledge Base:\n- The Detection server is in a **garbage collection (GC) cycle** (normal memory management) and may recover after several minutes.\n- The Detection server is undergoing a **maintenance operation**.\n- The Detection server is **unreachable due to a server failure**.\n\nWhat to do:\n- **Wait several minutes** if it may be GC-related; sensors connected to that server will **cache data locally** and send it once the server returns to normal.\n- If it **does not return to normal after 10–15 minutes**, or you have other indications of server failure, **contact Cybereason Technical Support**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021698: \"Failed to Connect Status for Detection Servers\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T19:21:11.000+0000)\n- Article #000021568: \"Sensor Not Connecting to Detection Server After Installing/Upgrading to 18.1 and above\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:13:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021141: \"How to Connect a New Detection Server to the UI\" (v3, updated 2025-09-22T20:11:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000021505: \"Sensor Connectivity Issues - Troubleshooting\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:03:17.000+0000)\n- Article #000022304: \"Troubleshooting Sensor Log Error Messages\" (v5, updated 2025-12-03T22:00:41.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why would Cybereason show 'failed to disinfect' on a malware alert?",
      "ground_truth": "It can happen because another application has the file open, preventing disinfection. Cybereason can’t force other apps to release the file handle.",
      "actual_answer": "Cybereason can show **“failed to disinfect”** when the Anti-Malware engine detects a malicious file but **can’t disinfect/delete it at that time because another application is holding an open handle to the file**.\n\nFrom the Knowledge Base, common clarifications are:\n\n- **Open file handles prevent disinfection:** If another process keeps the file open, Cybereason Anti-Malware **cannot force that application to release the file**, so disinfection fails.\n- **Risk is still mitigated:** The file **remains blocked until the machine reboots**, so it can’t be used to harm the system while in this state.\n- **Reboot usually completes cleanup:** The Anti-Malware driver **attempts to disinfect at reboot**, when it starts before most applications and the file is less likely to be locked.\n- **If reboot doesn’t resolve it:** The KB recommends **consulting IR to confirm it’s safe to remove the file manually**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021636: \"Failed to Disinfect Alert on Malware Screen\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T19:21:43.000+0000)\n- Article #000016846: \"Manage Malware Alerts\" (v4, updated 2025-11-24T21:12:53.000+0000)\n- Article #000021832: \"What Is the Difference Between Anti-Malware Detect and Disinfect Modes?\" (v2, updated 2025-07-08T21:36:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000021975: \"Why Am I Getting a \"Cybereason Anti-Malware solution installed on your system is cleaning your computer\" Message Upon Reboot?\" (v2, updated 2025-06-23T20:36:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000016860: \"Set the Anti-Malware Modes\" (v5, updated 2025-11-24T21:17:34.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why does a BitLocker USB stay visible for ~1 min even though USB block policy is on?",
      "ground_truth": "Endpoint Control only blocks USB devices after they are mounted. With BitLocker, the device mounts after the password is entered, and a once-per-minute enforcement thread may delay blocking up to a minute.",
      "actual_answer": "A BitLocker-encrypted USB can stay visible for up to ~1 minute because Cybereason’s Endpoint Controls blocks USB mass storage **after the device is mounted**, and BitLocker devices only mount **after the user enters the BitLocker password**.       "query": "Why do golden-image VM/VDI sensor clones show up twice or overwrite each other in Sensors?",
      "ground_truth": "This happens when multiple cloned sensors end up sharing the same PylumID, causing duplicate entries and data/connection overrides.",
      "actual_answer": "Golden-image VM/VDI sensor clones show up twice or overwrite each other in **System > Sensors** because **multiple cloned machines end up using the same sensor identifier (PylumID)**.\n\n- When sensors are deployed via a **golden image**, clones can retain the **original PylumID** instead of generating a new one.\n- If multiple sensors share the same PylumID:\n  - The **Sensors** screen can show **duplicate entries**\n  - Clones can **override each other’s data** and even **their connection to the server**\n\nWhat’s commonly behind this on Windows:\n- The sensor (ActiveConsole from 18.0+) checks whether the machine’s **NetBIOS name** is part of the PylumID. If it is, the clone may keep using the **previous PylumID** (shown as the **“Identifier”** value), especially if the clone’s unique machine name wasn’t set **before ActiveConsole starts**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021468: \"Duplicate Sensors or Data Overrides After VM or VDI Sensor Deployment with Golden Image\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:10:50.000+0000)\n- Article #000021499: \"Sensor on VM Connects and Disconnects\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:14:24.000+0000)\n- Article #000021330: \"Considerations for Deploying a Sensor Using a Golden Image\" (v1, updated 2025-06-09T21:12:32.000+0000)\n- Article #000016903: \"Clone Machines and Sensors using a Golden Image\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:33:54.000+0000)\n- Article #000022016: \"Virtualization FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-23T19:44:15.000+0000)\n- Article #000021340: \"Best Practices for VM and VDI Sensor Deployment: Golden Image With Unique PylumID\" (v2, updated 2025-07-09T16:37:11.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0925",
      "query": "Why do I see the same endpoint twice under System > Sensors?",
      "ground_truth": "Duplicates can appear if the machine disconnects and reconnects to a different Detection server, creating a new entry. They can also occur if the Sensor’s PylumID changes after an upgrade, wipe, or reinstall (often due to MAC address changes).",
      "actual_answer": "You’re seeing the same endpoint twice under **System > Sensors** because Cybereason can create a new sensor entry when the endpoint’s **sensor identifier (PylumID)** changes or when it reconnects in a way that results in a new entry.\n\nCommon causes described in the Knowledge Base:\n\n- **The endpoint reconnected to a different Detection server**\n  - If a machine disconnects from one Detection server and later connects to another, **a new entry is created**, resulting in duplicates.\n\n- **The sensor’s unique ID (PylumID) changed**\n  - This can happen after:\n    - **Upgrading the sensor**\n    - **Wiping/reimaging the machine and reinstalling the sensor**\n    - **A MAC address change** (PylumID is composed of **<organization name><machine name><MAC address>**)\n    - Reconnecting via a **different NIC**\n    - Initial/current connection occurring via **VPN** (as noted in the article’s examples)\n\nWhat to do:\n\n- In the listed scenarios above, **no action is necessary**; “the system works as designed.”\n- If duplicates are happening outside these scenarios and it’s impacting sensor management, **contact Cybereason Technical Support** for assistance.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021449: \"Duplicate Machines/Sensors Appear in the UI\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:09:58.000+0000)\n- Article #000021445: \"A Newly Installed Endpoint Sensor Does not Appear in the Cybereason UI\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:13:25.000+0000)\n- Article #000021406: \"Why Does the Investigation Screen Display Different Metadata for Similar Files on Different Sensors?\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:56:01.000+0000)\n- Article #000021468: \"Duplicate Sensors or Data Overrides After VM or VDI Sensor Deployment with Golden Image\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:10:50.000+0000)\n- Article #000022501: \"Mismatch - System/Sensors vs  investigation page - Get the Sensor Population\" (v5, updated 2025-12-03T20:14:23.000+0000)\n- Article #000022980: \"Restart Sensor\" (v3, updated 2025-10-31T19:24:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000023094: \"23.2 All Versions\" (v18, updated 2026-01-27T14:08:31.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0926",
      "query": "Why does MalOp Scope show more hosts than Affected Machines list?",
      "ground_truth": "The mismatch can happen because Affected Machines is calculated from MalOp Triage Data (suspicions) that has shorter retention, so deleted processes can remove associated machines from the list while Scope remains.",
      "actual_answer": "This discrepancy is expected by design because **Scope** and **Affected Machines** are calculated from different underlying data and have different retention/limits.\n\n- **Scope**\n  - Displays the MalOp’s scope when there is at least one affected machine or container.\n  - If more than one affected machine is involved, Scope can show an aggregated **machine count**.\n  - Scope is part of the **MalOp record (MalOp Core)** and is retained for the full MalOp Core retention period.\n\n- **Affected Machines list**\n  - Shows details for machines associated with the MalOp (name, GUID, count).\n  - This list is calculated based on **Suspicions** (part of **MalOp Triage Data**), which is retained for a **shorter period** than MalOp Core.\n\nCommon reasons Scope can show more hosts than the Affected Machines list:\n- **UI limit:** The MalOp details screen displays **up to 100 affected machines** (and 100 suspicious processes). This can reduce what appears in **Affected Machines** compared to the aggregated Scope count. (Cybereason can increase the limit via Technical Support, but does not recommend increasing the default due to potential performance impact.)\n- **Data retention:** If suspicious processes are deleted due to **MalOp Triage Data retention**, their associated machines can no longer be fetched for the graph/list—so **Affected Machines may shrink** over time—while **Scope remains**, since it’s retained as part of the MalOp element as long as the MalOp exists.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021542: \"Discrepancy Between Scope and Affected Machines in MalOp Details\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T19:08:55.000+0000)\n- Article #000023057: \"Update the Malop Investigation Status\" (v3, updated 2025-10-31T21:06:55.000+0000)\n- Article #000022154: \"Understanding the MalOp Details Timeline\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:28:14.000+0000)\n- Article #000021256: \"Duplicate MalOps Issue\" (v2, updated 2026-01-08T21:01:15.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0928",
      "query": "Detection server catalina.out shows Direct buffer OOM—what workaround steps fix it?",
      "ground_truth": "Stop Tomcat, back up the VC data files, delete the virtual cache .dat files (including index and schema VC files), then restart Tomcat.",
      "actual_answer": "To work around a **Detection Server `catalina.out` “java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Direct buffer memory”** issue, the Knowledge Base suggests clearing the Virtual Cache (VC) data files and restarting Tomcat.\n\n**Workaround steps**\n1. **Stop Tomcat**\n   - `sudo su`\n   - `service tomcat stop`\n\n2. **Back up VC data files**\n   - `mkdir /tmp/backup_data`\n   - `cp -rp /opt/cybereason/detection/index /tmp/backup_data/`\n   - `cp -rp /opt/cybereason/detection/schema /tmp/backup_data/`\n\n3. **Delete VC data files**\n   - `rm -rf /virtual_cache/*.dat`\n   - `rm -rf /opt/cybereason/detection/index/*.dat`\n   - `rm -rf /opt/cybereason/detection/schema/virtualCacheFeatureSchema.dat`\n   - `rm -rf /opt/cybereason/detection/schema/historic/virtualCacheFeatureSchema.dat.*`\n\n4. **Start services**\n   - `service iptables restart`\n   - `service tomcat start`\n\n**What the KB does/doesn’t say**\n- The KB lists the cause as **Unknown** and provides the above as a **possible workaround**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021559: \"Detection Server Error : OutOfMemoryError: Direct buffer Memory\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:07:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000021772: \"Sensor UI Shows All Sensors as Offline\" (v2, updated 2025-09-05T20:25:36.000+0000)\n- Article #000021100: \"How to Disable Catalina.out Logging\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:34:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021141: \"How to Connect a New Detection Server to the UI\" (v3, updated 2025-09-22T20:11:47.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "It happens when you remove the default registry keys from the inclusions grid but don’t add any inclusion keys back to the grid.",
      "actual_answer": "Deleted default registry inclusion keys reappear after a Detection server refresh/restart because the Cybereason platform automatically repopulates the **default registry event collection inclusions** (autorun-related keys) when the inclusions grid is **empty**.\n\n- **Cause:** You deleted the default inclusions but did **not** add at least one inclusion entry afterward.  \n- **Behavior:** If the grid is left blank, the platform restores the default keys on Detection server restart/refresh.  \n- **Fix/Prevention:** Add **any** registry key inclusion so the grid is not empty (some articles note you can add a dummy/non-existent key, though Cybereason does not recommend removing the default keys because they’re commonly used by malware).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021455: \"Deleted Registry Keys Added back to the Grid\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:07:11.000+0000)\n- Article #000021811: \"Which Registry Keys are Collected that Relate to Persistence?\" (v2, updated 2025-07-08T21:52:40.000+0000)\n- Article #000022211: \"Troubleshooting the Registry Events Collection Configuration\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T21:51:28.000+0000)\n- Article #000016345: \"Configure Additional Collections\" (v3, updated 2026-01-12T23:08:01.000+0000)\n- Article #000022749: \"Registry Event Collection Default Enablement - Feature Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "To clear stuck `CLOSE_WAIT` sessions on port **1337** that prevent the **Cyber console** from opening, stop **Tomcat**, wait for the sessions to clear, then reconfigure/restart the server.\n\n1. **Confirm stuck sessions on port 1337**\n   - Run:\n     - `netstat -nap | grep CLOSE_WAIT`\n   - You will typically see entries like `127.0.0.1:1337 ... CLOSE_WAIT`.\n\n2. **Stop Tomcat**\n   - Run:\n     - `service tomcat stop`\n\n3. **Wait until sessions clear (do not restart immediately)**\n   - Keep checking until the list is empty:\n     - `netstat -nap | grep CLOSE_WAIT`\n   - **Important:** When Tomcat is stopped, you must wait for the application to clean all stuck sessions—**don’t start it immediately**.\n\n4. **Start/recover the server**\n   - Run:\n     - `/opt/puppet-cybereason/reconfigure.sh`\n\nIf there are **no stuck sessions** and it’s not urgent, the KB also notes an alternative: **open a NOC case to restart the instance at night right after the automatic snapshot is taken**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021027: \"Cyber Console Stuck\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T18:55:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000020966: \"How to Restart the Detection server (Cloud)\" (v2, updated 2025-12-22T19:51:46.000+0000)\n- Article #000016814: \"Respond to Threats on a Machine with Remote Shell\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:01:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000011678: \"Collect Server Log Data and Network Traffic\" (v3, updated 2025-11-14T20:25:51.000+0000)\n- Article #000017324: \"Collect Server Log Data and Network Traffic\" (v3, updated 2025-11-14T19:50:57.000+0000)",

      "query": "Periodic kernel module collection: when does a module get end time after it disappears?",
      "ground_truth": "In periodic collection, if a module is no longer observed, it expires 10 seconds later and then its end time is set and published.",
      "actual_answer": "In **periodic kernel module collection**, a module gets an **end time 10 seconds after it is no longer seen** in the periodic scan.\n\n- The sensor periodically iterates over **all currently loaded modules**.\n- **As long as a module is seen**, its “lifetime” in the sensor’s internal DB is extended.\n- **Once a module is not seen anymore**, it **expires 10 seconds later** and then the sensor **determines and publishes the end time**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000022775: \"Advanced Kernel Modules Collection - Feature Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-12-03T18:51:02.000+0000)\n- Article #000022735: \"Process Collection Improvements - Feature Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "Stale/archived sensor email alerts are controlled by a global setting. If enabled, System administrators and Sensor admin L1 users receive them regardless of individual notification preferences.",
      "actual_answer": "Admins can still receive stale/archived sensor emails because **these notifications are controlled by a global stale/archived sensor email setting**, not by each user’s individual **Notification settings**.\n\n- **Stale/archived sensor emails are managed separately** from other email notification preferences.\n- If **Enable email notifications for stale sensors** and/or **Enable email notifications for archived sensors** is set to **On**, then **System administrators (and Sensor admin L1 users)** will receive these emails **even if** the user’s **Enable notification** checkbox is not selected on the **Users** screen.\n- The archived sensors report email may be sent **even when there are 0 stale/archived sensors**, and will state that 0 sensors are archived.\n\nTo stop these emails, disable the relevant global toggles in the stale/archived sensor settings (e.g., turn off **Enable email notifications for stale sensors** / **archived sensors**).\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021512: \"Cannot Remove Email Address from the Archived Sensors Report\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:46:29.000+0000)\n- Article #000016789: \"Remove Sensors from Monitoring\" (v7, updated 2025-12-12T12:31:02.000+0000)\n- Article #000015736: \"Stale and Archived Sensors\" (v2, updated 2025-12-18T21:02:07.000+0000)\n- Article #000023123: \"18.0 Release Fixed Issues\" (v4, updated 2025-11-07T23:21:54.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "Next steps depend on whether the issue is a **failed MSI-based sensor upgrade** or a broader **connectivity/distribution problem**.\n\n- **Confirm whether this is an MSI-signature issue on Windows 10**\n  - If the endpoint is **Windows 10** and the upgrade package is an **MSI** (minor upgrade/HF/SP), the upgrade can fail due to **Windows update KB4565351** rejecting the MSI signature (because Cybereason appends personalization data after signing).\n  - **Fix:** upgrade using a sensor version that includes the hotfix (Windows 10 only): **19.1.282+, 19.2.182+, 20.1.327+, 20.1.342+, or 20.2.20+**.\n  - Note: This issue applies to **MSI packages only** (not EXE).\n\n- **Check whether sensors are still attempting to connect (to rule in/out connectivity issues)**\n  - On the relevant machine/network, capture traffic to see if the Probe is trying to reach the server:\n    - `tcpdump -s0 -iany -wout.cap`\n  - In Wireshark, filter for:\n    - `ip.addr == <PROBE_EXTERNAL_IP>` (if known), **or**\n    - `tcp.port == <PROBES_LISTEN_PORT>`\n  - Look for **SYN** (connect attempts) from Probe to Server and **FIN** (disconnects).\n    - If the **Server** appears to be disconnecting, check server logs for errors/exceptions; if found, **contact R&D** (per the guide).\n    - If there are **no server-side errors**, it’s likely a **firewall** issue—review the customer firewall setup.\n\n- **If you see “MsiSendFail” on the Detection Server**\n  - Check the Detection Server `catalina.out` for the **MsiSendFail** error, which indicates a failure while sending the MSI upgrade package.\n\nWhat I can’t confirm from the retrieved content: the exact UI workflow to retry/resend the MSI package or specific remediation steps for **MsiSendFail** beyond checking `catalina.out`—those details aren’t included in the provided KB excerpts.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021376: \"Sensor upgrade fails with Error: Bad MSI Signature on Windows 10 - Support Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-07-10T16:58:34.000+0000)\n- Article #000021583: \"Common Connectivity Problems (Sensor) - Troubleshoot Guide\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:50:20.000+0000)\n- Article #000021635: \"Sensor Upgrade Fails with Error Message \"MsiSendFail\" in Detection Server catalina.out Log\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T22:00:05.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "The user must have the **`listFiles`** role in MongoDB for the **Browse Files** option to appear.\n\n- Check the user’s roles on the Perspective/UI server MongoDB:\n  - `mongo cybereason`\n  - `db.cyber.users.find({\"_id\" : \"user-email-address@user-domain.com\"}).pretty()`\n- Verify `listFiles` is present under `roles`.\n- If it’s missing, add it while preserving the user’s existing roles (example from KB):\n  - `db.cyber.users.update({\"_id\" : \"user-email-address@user-domain.com\"}, {$set: {\"roles\" : [\"user_admin\",\"sys_admin\",\"analyst_l3\",\"responder\",\"listFiles\"]}})`\n  - Replace the roles list with the user’s actual existing roles + `listFiles`.\n- Have the user **log out and log back in**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021162: \"Browse Files Option Missing\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:45:18.000+0000)\n- Article #000020878: \"How to Enable and Disable File Search\" (v3, updated 2025-12-01T21:43:33.000+0000)\n- Article #000022733: \"Browse Files Dynamic Configuration - Feature Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000021910: \"File Search, File Browse and File Download FAQ\" (v2, updated 2025-06-16T15:35:40.000+0000)\n- Article #000016715: \"Browse Files on Machines\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T17:48:59.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why are canary files showing up on shared network drives if Cybereason didn't put them there?",
      "ground_truth": "Cybereason doesn’t create canary files in shared network folders. If they appear there, they were likely copied or synced from a local machine via redirection, Offline Files, backups, or scripts.",
      "actual_answer": "Cybereason doesn’t deploy canary files to **network drives/shared folders**—if you see them there, they were **copied or synchronized from an endpoint’s local canary locations** by another mechanism.\n\nCommon reasons canary files end up on shared network drives include:\n- **Folder Redirection Group Policy** copying user folders (and their contents) to a network location\n- **Windows Offline Files** synchronizing local folders to a network share\n- **Backup software or scripts** (copy jobs) that replicate hidden/system files to shared resources\n\nWhat you can do:\n- **Safely delete** the canary files from the network share (they were not created/used by Cybereason there).\n- To stop them from returning, identify and prevent the replication source:\n  - Exclude **hidden files/folders** from backup tools\n  - Disable or update **custom copy scripts** to exclude hidden files/folders\n  - Disable **Folder Redirection Group Policy** (if possible)\n  - Disable **Windows Offline Files**\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021432: \"Canary Files Appearing in Shared Network Folders\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:41:26.000+0000)\n- Article #000016856: \"Canary Files\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:16:19.000+0000)\n- Article #000021521: \"Canary Files Being Synchronized to Cloud Storage\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:42:01.000+0000)\n- Article #000021510: \"Many Canary Folders in a Single Directory\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:12:13.000+0000)",

      "actual_answer": "To stop Cybereason canary files from syncing into OneDrive/Dropbox (or other cloud-sync folders), you need to prevent Cybereason from deploying canary files into folders that your cloud storage client syncs (commonly **Desktop** or **Documents**), or move the cloud-sync directory to a location not protected by canary files.\n\n- **Option 1 (Cybereason-side): Disable canary file deployment to the synced folder**\n  - In the **sensor policy**, go to **Anti-Ransomware > Canary files > Folders**.\n  - **Clear** the folder location(s) that map to your OneDrive/Dropbox sync area (typically **Desktop** and/or **Users documents**).\n\n- **Option 2 (Cloud storage-side): Change the sync directory**\n  - In OneDrive/Dropbox settings on the endpoint, **change the local sync directory** to a folder that Cybereason is **not** deploying canary files to (refer to your cloud provider’s documentation for the steps).\n\n- **Important note (from Cybereason):**\n  - There is a **protection trade-off**: limiting canary file locations may reduce ransomware detection effectiveness, and Cybereason notes this is **not recommended** unless necessary.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021521: \"Canary Files Being Synchronized to Cloud Storage\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:42:01.000+0000)\n- Article #000021510: \"Many Canary Folders in a Single Directory\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:12:13.000+0000)\n- Article #000016853: \"Set the Canary File-Based Anti-Ransomware Modes\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:15:45.000+0000)\n- Article #000021432: \"Canary Files Appearing in Shared Network Folders\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:41:26.000+0000)\n- Article #000011330: \"Configure Anti-Ransomware Settings (Canary Files)\" (v2, updated 2025-11-20T18:08:05.000+0000)\n- Article #000016856: \"Canary Files\" (v3, updated 2025-11-24T21:16:19.000+0000)",

      "ground_truth": "If the TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED error persists in the Detection server catalina.out logs, open a NOC case and ask them to re-run the specified Data Infra onboarding Jenkins job for that environment.",
      "actual_answer": "To fix `TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED` / `TopicAuthorizationException` errors in `catalina.out` on the Detection server (DI environments), you need to have TechOps/NOC re-run the Data Infra full-stack Jenkins job for the affected environment. If the auth error clears but Investigation data is still missing, re-export Machine/User elements from each Detection server to DI.\n\n### What to do\n1. **Confirm the error**\n   - In the Detection server `catalina.out`, look for messages like:\n     - `TopicAuthorizationException: Not authorized to access topics: [<topic>]`\n     - `{<topic>=TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED}`\n\n2. **Open a NOC/TechOps case to re-run the DI onboarding/full-stack job**\n   - If the `TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED` error continues, open a NOC case and request re-running this Jenkins job for your environment:\n     - `http://jenkins-prod.cybereason.net:8080/view/production-jobs/view/Jobs-for-TechOps/job/Data-infra-onboarding-central/job/Data-Infra-Full-Stack-Customer-Wrapper/`\n\n3. **If the auth error is gone but Investigation data is still missing, re-export to DI (DI+VC example)**\n   - SSH to **each** Detection server and run:\n     - `curl -kL https://localhost:18443/transparency/rest/vc/exporter/exportAll/Machine`\n     - `curl -kL https://localhost:18443/transparency/rest/vc/exporter/exportAll/User`\n   - Repeat on all Detection servers.\n\n### What this addresses\n- This KB specifically ties `TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED` to the Detection server failing to export data to Data Infra (DI), resulting in missing EDR data in the **Investigation** screen.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021728: \"Authorization Error on Kafka Topic\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:27:28.000+0000)\n- Article #000022225: \"Data Infra Alerts and Troubleshooting\" (v5, updated 2025-12-03T19:05:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000021099: \"How to Update Expired DI Certificates\" (v2, updated 2025-12-29T18:24:07.000+0000)",

you need to **open a support case** to have it reviewed/applied.\n\n- **Query limit issue when you have more than 500 sensors**\n  - There is a known issue where clicking the number of sensors assigned to a policy can show **zero or only a few sensors** due to a **query limit (500)**;       "actual_answer": "If an NGAV (Anti-Malware) installation stays **In Progress** after you previously **uninstalled the sensor**, the Cybereason Knowledge Base indicates the fix is to **restart the machine** so the pending post-uninstall changes can complete.\n\n- **Restart the endpoint**\n  - After reboot, check the Cybereason console: **System > Sensors**\n  - You should see a notification like **“Restart is required for this machine”** until the reboot is done, and the installation should complete afterward.\n\nIf the uninstall itself previously failed with an error indicating a reboot is required (e.g., **0x8007015e – No action was taken as a system reboot is required**), then:\n- **Reboot the system**\n- **Rerun the uninstall procedure** (if needed) and then proceed with the installation again.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021465: \"Anti-Malware Installation Does Not Complete\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:20:10.000+0000)\n- Article #000021722: \"Sensor Install Hangs or is Unresponsive\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:07:28.000+0000)\n- Article #000021795: \"Sensor Uninstall Fails with an Error\" (v3, updated 2025-09-05T20:27:28.000+0000)\n- Article #000021476: \"Sensor Status Remains Offline after Sensor is Upgraded\" (v3, updated 2026-03-18T13:15:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021482: \"Sensor Uninstall from Add/Remove Programs Fails\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:22:25.000+0000)\n- Article #000021642: \"Anti-Malware Service Fails to Update Following New Sensor Installation\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:20:25.000+0000)\n- Article #000021475: \"Sensor with Signatures mode Enabled Stuck in Initializing State\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:24:16.000+0000)\n- Article #000021444: \"Mac AV Does Not Prevent Malware After Installation\" (v2, updated 2025-07-17T21:40:31.000+0000)",

      "query": "Why do detection servers flip to 'Failed to Connect' after deleting a site mid-migration?",
      "ground_truth": "If the site is removed before sensors are fully reassigned, sensors flood back to the prior detection servers. This overload triggers small GC cycles, causing intermittent connectivity and 'Failed to Connect' in the UI.",
      "actual_answer": "Detection servers flip to **“Failed to Connect”** after deleting a site mid-migration because **sensors that were still in the process of being reassigned suddenly “flood” back to their previous Detection servers**, overloading them.\n\nFrom the Knowledge Base context:\n\n- When the site is **abruptly removed before sensors have fully reassigned**, the sensors reconnect en masse to the prior Detection servers.\n- This sudden burst can **overload the Detection servers**, causing them to enter **frequent garbage collection (GC) cycles**.\n- While in GC cycles, Detection servers may only connect to the WebApp/Perspective server **briefly**, then drop again—so in **System > Servers** they appear as **“Failed to connect”** or flip between online and failed.\n- More generally, **“Failed to connect”** indicates the Detection server **failed to connect to the WebApp server**, commonly due to **GC cycles**, maintenance, or an actual server failure.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021596: \"After Site was Deleted All Servers Display \"Failed to Connect\"\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:20:04.000+0000)\n- Article #000021698: \"Failed to Connect Status for Detection Servers\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T19:21:11.000+0000)\n- Article #000021673: \"UI/Detection/Registration Servers Not Starting with Error Message \"Timed out while waiting to connect after 1000 ms\"\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:52:42.000+0000)\n- Article #000022304: \"Troubleshooting Sensor Log Error Messages\" (v5, updated 2025-12-03T22:00:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000021505: \"Sensor Connectivity Issues - Troubleshooting\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:03:17.000+0000)",
      "correctness": 5,

      "faithfulness": 4,
      "verdict": "pass",

Adds some extra general troubleshooting statements (maintenance/actual failure) not in the reference, but they don’t contradict the core explanation.",

      "query": "Why would MalOp report emails stop sending to one address in Mandrill?",
      "ground_truth": "Mandrill marks the address as Rejected and stops sending because it was added to the Rejection Blacklist due to a soft or hard bounce.",
      "actual_answer": "MalOp report emails can stop sending to a specific address in Mandrill if Mandrill has **rejected** that recipient due to a prior **bounce** (soft bounce or hard bounce), which places the address on Mandrill’s **Rejection Blacklist (Denylist)**.\n\nTo confirm and fix:\n- In the **Mandrill UI**, go to **Settings > Rejection List > Rejection Blacklist (Denylist)**.\n- Find the affected email address to see details like the **blacklist reason** and **expiration date**.\n- If needed, **remove** the email address from the **Rejection Blacklist (Denylist)** to allow sending again.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021573: \"[Mandrill] MalOp Report Stops Working for Specific Email Address\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:05:52.000+0000)\n- Article #000020960: \"How to Access Mandrill SMTP Server\" (v3, updated 2025-11-25T22:05:50.000+0000)\n- Article #000021667: \"Malop Report Tracker - Feature Handoff\" (v2, updated 2025-07-18T20:45:41.000+0000)\n- Article #000021713: \"Failed to Send MalOp Notification to Mailing List Due to Problems in Mailing Service\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T19:22:56.000+0000)\n- Article #000021566: \"MalOp Report Stops Working\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T20:09:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000022797: \"XDR MalOp Correlation Engine - Feature Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)",

      "query_id": "tc_0984",
      "query": "Why would an allowlisted hash still get quarantined on some endpoints?",
      "ground_truth": "Allowlist changes sync to sensors only after they connect and pull the updated configuration. If a sensor was offline during the update, it may still trigger protection events until it comes online and syncs.",
      "actual_answer": "An allowlisted hash can still get quarantined on some endpoints because the allowlist update may not yet be synchronized to those specific sensors, or because the quarantine happened before the allowlist took effect (and existing quarantined items are not automatically reversed).\n\nKey reasons described in the Knowledge Base:\n\n- **Allowlist propagation delay to sensors**\n  - Allowlists can take time to sync to all online sensors.\n  - After you add a hash to the allowlist, online sensors will *usually* stop quarantining/detecting/protecting it **within a few hours**.\n  - If an endpoint hasn’t received the updated allowlist DB version yet, it may still quarantine the file.\n\n- **The endpoint may not have been online to receive the update**\n  - To confirm, check the affected sensor’s logs for an allowlist DB version update message, e.g.:\n    - `new ransomware.db_version database version ...`\n    - `... db ... hashes in 1 mode`\n  - If those messages don’t appear after the allowlist change, the sensor likely didn’t receive the update.\n\n- **Existing quarantines are not automatically undone**\n  - Updating the allowlist affects **future** detections/protections only.\n  - **Existing quarantined file entries are not affected**; you must **unquarantine or remediate separately** (Cybereason does not trigger unquarantine actions based on an allowlist update for the same hash).\n\nWhat to verify quickly:\n\n1. Confirm the hash is actually present in the console allowlist/custom reputation list (Private reputations):  \n   `https://your-env.cybereason.net/#/security-profile/reputations-list`\n2. On an endpoint that is still quarantining, check sensor logs for receipt of the new allowlist DB version (examples above).\n3. If the hash is allowlisted and the endpoint is online but still quarantines after the sensor shows it received the updated DB version, the KB recommends **opening a case with R&D** to investigate.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021721: \"A Protection Event is Executed for Allowlisted Files\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:15:02.000+0000)\n- Article #000022762: \"Automatically Add Unquarantined Files to the Allowlist - Feature Handoff\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T19:56:15.000+0000)\n- Article #000021528: \"Application Control Repeatedly Prevents an Application from Running\" (v4, updated 2025-12-03T18:21:21.000+0000)\n- Article #000021797: \"Which Cybereason Components Support Hash-based Allow/Blocklisting?\" (v2, updated 2025-07-08T21:49:17.000+0000)",

      "query": "CSV import says file invalid during sensor rebalancing—what fixes it?",

      "actual_answer": "To fix **“The file you uploaded is invalid”** during **sensor rebalancing CSV import**, check the CSV content first, and then verify the **Site (“Region”) names** exist—missing sites (commonly **Default**) are a known cause.\n\n## Fix steps\n\n### 1) Validate the rebalancing CSV format/content\nIn the CSV you upload for rebalancing, confirm:\n\n- **No duplicate FQDNs**\n- **No blank/empty cells**\n- **No invalid Site names** (use the exact names shown in **Manage sites**)\n- **No invalid Detection server names** (use the exact names shown on the **Detection servers** page)\n- **Header row is present**\n- Only the required columns remain (per the rebalancing workflow):  \n  **FQDN, Site, Server name, OS, OS Version**\n\n### 2) Check for a missing Site (common “Default” issue)\nIf the **Default** site wasn’t actually created (it can be skipped if it looks like it already exists), the upload can fail.\n\n- Click **Test Configuration** and check the UI server `catalina.out` for a warning like:  \n  `The region Default not exist in the regions list for the configuration file`\n\nIf you see that warning, the fix is:\n\n- **Create the missing Site** (e.g., **Default**) in **Manage sites**\n- **Generate a new CSV** assigning sensors to the **correct (existing) Site**\n- Re-upload the new CSV\n\n## If it fails only after clicking “Test configuration”\nThe Knowledge Base notes that an error after clicking **Test configuration** “generally indicates a server issue.” If the CSV checks out and sites are correct, you may need Cybereason Support to investigate server-side errors.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021694: \"\"The File You Uploaded is Invalid\" Error Displays While Importing CSV File\" (v4, updated 2025-12-01T22:04:06.000+0000)\n-       "query": "SSO login shows callback URL mismatch—what setting usually missing in Auth0?",
      "ground_truth": "The Auth0 application settings are missing the WebApp port (8443) in the Allowed Callback/Logout URLs. Add the port under Application URIs and save changes.",
      "actual_answer": "The **WebApp port (typically `:8443`) is usually missing** from the Auth0 application’s **Allowed Callback URLs** (and often **Allowed Logout URLs**), causing the redirect/callback URL to not match.\n\n- This happens when your Cybereason environment must be accessed with a URL like:\n  - `https://<tenant>.cybereason.net:8443/`\n- If Auth0 is configured with the same URL **without** `:8443`, Auth0 returns **“Callback URL mismatch… redirect_uri is not in the list of allowed callback URLs.”**\n\n**Fix (in Auth0):**\n1. Open the relevant Auth0 tenant (US: `cybereason-us-prod`, EU/APAC: `cybereason-eu-prod`).\n2. Go to **Applications > Applications** and open the customer’s application.\n3. Under **Application URIs**, add/update **Allowed Callback URLs** (and **Allowed Logout URLs**) to include the URL **with `:8443`**.\n4. **Save Changes**.\n\nSources:\n- Article #000021744: \"\"Oops! something went wrong\" Error Returned After Clicking 'Sign in with SSO'\" (v4, updated 2025-12-01T22:03:47.000+0000)\n- Article #000022323: \"Needed Information for SSO Feature Configuration\" (v2, updated 2025-08-20T17:55:16.000+0000)\n- Article #000022641: \"Single Sign-On (SSO) Handoff\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:19:31.000+0000)\n- Article #000021456: \"User Redirected to Auth0 Error Page when attempting to Sign in Using SSO\" (v3, updated 2025-12-03T21:56:48.000+0000)\n- Article #000022451: \"Update the SSO Configuration in your Defender Console\" (v2, updated 2025-10-15T16:50:16.000+0000)\n- Article #000021038: \"How to Create an Application in Auth0 - SSO\" (v2, updated 2025-12-08T19:38:09.000+0000)\n- Article #000022449: \"Retrieve SSO Configuration Details\" (v1, updated 2025-06-10T14:28:50.000+0000)",
